title_original: Palermo, la Fondazione Sant’Elia si rilancia come polo del contemporaneo
editorial_title_zh: 巴勒莫圣埃利亚基金会转型为当代艺术中心
editorial_excerpt_zh: 巴勒莫圣埃利亚基金会（Fondazione Sant’Elia）在当代艺术与研究项目之间开启了新征程：首先推出一场汇聚意大利及国际艺术家的宏大展览 本文“巴勒莫圣埃利亚基金会转型为当代艺术中心”来源于…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴勒莫圣埃利亚基金会正迎来一个新的体制与文化发展阶段。该机构自2010年活跃至今，致力于巩固其国际影响力，并制定专注当代创意的规划，尤其关注艺术、历史与地中海之间的关系。在巴勒莫大都会市（Città Metropolitana di Palermo）主席罗伯托·拉加拉（Roberto Lagalla）的推动下——该参考机构负责任命基金会的领导层与董事会——此次转型也从治理层面展开，由2026年4月被任命的主席爱德华多·德菲利皮斯（Eduardo De Filippis）领导，并由总监督帕特里齐亚·蒙特罗索（Patrizia Monterosso）负责指导。董事会则由安吉拉·芬达罗（Angela Fundarò）、达尼洛·马尼斯卡尔科（Danilo Maniscalco）、弗朗切斯科·邦加拉（Francesco Bongarrà）和玛丽亚·萨埃利（Maria Saeli）组成。", "links": [{"text": "Fondazione Sant’Elia", "url": "https://www.fondazionesantelia.it/"}, {"text": "Palermo", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/palermo/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "圣埃利亚基金会，立足巴勒莫与地中海之间", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "基金会旨在通过开放且跨学科的策展模式，巩固其作为艺术家、策展人、学者以及国内外机构之间创作与交流中心的地位。圣埃利亚基金会于2010年底由当时的巴勒莫地区省政府发起成立，旨在推广艺术文化并提升本土遗产的价值。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "自2013年起，基金会的两个场馆——圣埃利亚宫（Palazzo Sant’Elia）与圣巴托洛梅奥拱廊（Loggiato di San Bartolomeo）——主要用作举办临时展览的空间。新架构将扩大这一功能，在展览活动之余，增设研究、培训和文化生产项目，包括展览、驻留艺术家项目、座谈会、工作坊以及与学校、大学、美术学院和研究中心合作开展的教育项目。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "协调这一阶段工作的将是帕特里齐亚·蒙特罗索（Patrizia Monterosso），她是一位文化管理者，此前曾领导腓特烈二世基金会（Fondazione Federico II）以及致力于文化和社会包容领域的RIV基金会。这一新征程还将伴随基金会全新视觉身份的确立。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Palazzo-S.Elia_Cortile-onore_-foto-Marcello-Messineo.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "圣埃利亚宫，荣誉庭院，马尔切洛·梅西内奥（Marcello Messineo）摄影", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "“黄金时刻”，开启新征程的展览", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "首个试金石是展览《黄金时刻：多变感知》（Ora d’oro. Percezioni variabili），计划于2026年11月14日至2027年4月15日在圣埃利亚宫举办。展览将汇集米罗斯瓦夫·巴尔卡（Mirosław Bałka）、约纳斯·布尔格特（Jonas Burgert）、马丁·埃德（Martin Eder）、西尔维娅·贾姆布罗内（Silvia Giambrone）、伊利亚与埃米莉亚·卡巴科夫（Ilya ed Emilia Kabakov）、希林·奈沙（Shirin Neshat）、阿尔弗雷多·皮里（Alfredo Pirri）、安塞尔姆·赖勒（Anselm Reyle）和托马斯·舒特（Thomas Schütte）的作品。策展委员会由切萨雷·比亚西尼·塞尔瓦吉（Cesare Biasini Selvaggi）、詹卢卡·科利卡（Gianluca Collica）和帕特里齐亚·蒙特罗索（Patrizia Monterosso）组成。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该展览从对区分现实与表象之难度的反思出发，剖析这两个长期交织的领域。该项目直面一个充斥着冲突、动荡以及共同参考标准危机的当下，同时也面对影像泛滥和日益加速的通信形式。在此背景下，感知被视为一种不稳定的状态，极易遭受操纵、奇观化和简单化的影响。受邀艺术家们需要直面这些议题，而圣埃利亚宫的18世纪建筑则直接融入了观展路线的构建之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "两个场馆：圣埃利亚宫与圣巴托洛梅奥拱廊", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "基金会的新阶段不可避免地也与其总部的历史紧密相连。位于马克达街（via Maqueda）的圣埃利亚宫在18世纪下半叶呈现出当前的风貌，当时乔万巴蒂斯塔·切斯特里和圣克鲁斯格里马尔迪（Giovanbattista Celestri e Grimaldi di Santa Croce）决定对一座早期的16至17世纪建筑进行扩建。自1759年起，工程由乔万巴蒂斯塔·卡斯蒂奥内（Giovanbattista Cascione）主持指导，使这座建筑群成为该市最宏伟的宫殿之一。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "随着时间的推移，这座建筑曾承担过多种截然不同的用途：它曾是参议院所在地、皇家农业、艺术与制造业鼓励研究所（Reale Istituto per l’incoraggiamento d’agricoltura, arti e manifatture）、铁路管理局的所在地，并在20世纪成为了朱塞佩·韦尔加（Giuseppe Verga）初级中学。它于1984年被省政府收购并随后修缮，自2013年起交由圣埃利亚基金会管理，并作为展览场馆向公众开放。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Loggiato_San_Bartolomeo.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "圣巴托洛梅奥拱廊", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "位于维托里奥·埃马努埃莱大道（corso Vittorio Emanuele）、距离菲利切门（Porta Felice）仅几步之遥并俯瞰意大利广场（Foro Italico）的圣巴托洛梅奥拱廊，则有着更为悠久的历史。该建筑群最初是圣巴托洛梅奥医院的一部分，由同名兄弟会在13世纪上半叶创立。在1943年5月轰炸中遭受严重损毁的古老医院的各个建筑体中，这座由同名兄弟会创立的双层16世纪拱廊幸存了下来，其特点是底层为半圆拱，上层为曲线轮廓的开口，并以镂空栏杆收尾。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "经过修复后，该拱廊于1998年重新对公众开放，并逐渐展现出对当代艺术的强烈使命，曾举办过塔诺·费斯塔（Tano Festa）、雷纳托·曼博尔（Renato Mambor）、埃米利奥·格雷科（Emilio Greco）、贾科莫·曼祖（Giacomo Manzù）、佩德罗·卡诺（Pedro Cano）、克罗切·塔拉韦拉（Croce Taravella）、朱塞佩·莫迪卡（Giuseppe Modica）、皮耶罗·古焦内（Piero Guccione）、格雷戈里奥·博塔（Gregorio Botta）和伊戈尔·米托拉伊（Igor Mitoraj）等艺术家的展览。米托拉伊更是在该建筑群西翼前留下了一件名为《埃利米安英雄》（Eroe elimo）的青铜纪念雕塑，以此献给这座城市的古地中海历史。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "自2025年6月起，该拱廊已被移交回大都会市，以便开展在国家复苏和韧性计划（PNRRL）框架下获得资助的重修工程，其主要目的是改善无障碍通行条件。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
La Fondazione Sant’Elia di Palermo avvia una nuova fase istituzionale e culturale. L’ente, attivo dal 2010, punta a rafforzare la propria dimensione internazionale e a sviluppare una programmazione dedicata alla creatività contemporanea, con particolare attenzione al rapporto tra arte, storia e Mediterraneo. Su impulso di Roberto Lagalla , presidente della Città Metropolitana di Palermo, ente di riferimento che nomina i vertici istituzionali e il Consiglio di Amministrazione della Fondazione, il rilancio è partito anche dalla governance, con la guida dal presidente Eduardo De Filippis , nominato ad aprile 2026, e la direzione della sovrintendente Patrizia Monterosso . Il Cda è invece composto da Angela Fundarò, Danilo Maniscalco, Francesco Bongarrà e Maria Saeli .

Fondazione Sant’Elia, tra Palermo e il Mediterraneo

La Fondazione intende consolidare il proprio ruolo come centro di produzione e confronto tra artisti, curatori, studiosi e istituzioni nazionali e internazionali, attraverso un modello curatoriale aperto e interdisciplinare. La Fondazione Sant’Elia nacque alla fine del 2010 per volontà dell’allora Provincia regionale di Palermo con lo scopo di promuovere arte e cultura e valorizzare il patrimonio del territorio.

Dal 2013, le due sedi della Fondazione, Palazzo Sant’Elia e il Loggiato di San Bartolomeo, sono stati utilizzati soprattutto come spazi per mostre temporanee. Il nuovo assetto amplierà questa funzione, affiancando all’attività espositiva progetti di ricerca, formazione e produzione culturale, tra mostre, residenze d’artista, talk, workshop e progetti educativi realizzati in collaborazione con scuole, università, accademie di belle arti e centri di ricerca.

A coordinare questa fase sarà Patrizia Monterosso, manager culturale con precedenti esperienze alla guida della Fondazione Federico II e della Fondazione RIV, realtà impegnata nei campi della cultura e dell’inclusione sociale. Al nuovo corso sarà associata anche una nuova identità visiva della Fondazione.

Ora d’oro, la mostra che apre il nuovo corso

Il primo banco di prova sarà la mostra Ora d’oro. Percezioni variabili , in programma dal 14 novembre 2026 al 15 aprile 2027 a Palazzo Sant’Elia. L’esposizione riunirà le opere di Mirosław Bałka, Jonas Burgert, Martin Eder, Silvia Giambrone, Ilya ed Emilia Kabakov, Shirin Neshat, Alfredo Pirri, Anselm Reyle e Thomas Schütte . Il board curatoriale è composto da Cesare Biasini Selvaggi, Gianluca Collica e Patrizia Monterosso .

La mostra si sviluppa a partire da una riflessione sulla difficoltà nel distinguere tra realtà e rappresentazione, separando due ambiti da sempre intrecciati. Il progetto affronta un presente segnato da conflitti, instabilità e crisi dei riferimenti condivisi ma anche dalla sovrapproduzione delle immagini e da forme di comunicazione sempre più accelerate. In questo contesto, la percezione viene assunta come una condizione instabile, esposta alla manipolazione, alla spettacolarizzazione e alla semplificazione. Gli artisti invitati sono chiamati a confrontarsi con tali questioni, mentre l’architettura settecentesca di Palazzo Sant’Elia entra direttamente nella costruzione del percorso.

Le due sedi: Palazzo Sant’Elia e il Loggiato di San Bartolomeo

La nuova fase della Fondazione passa inevitabilmente anche dalla storia della propria sede principale. Palazzo Sant’Elia, in via Maqueda, assunse l’attuale configurazione nella seconda metà del Settecento, quando Giovanbattista Celestri e Grimaldi di Santa Croce decise di ampliare un precedente edificio cinque-seicentesco. Dal 1759 i lavori furono diretti da Giovanbattista Cascione , contribuendo a trasformare il complesso in uno dei palazzi più imponenti della città.

Nel tempo l’edificio ha avuto destinazioni molto differenti: è stato sede del Senato, del Reale Istituto per l’incoraggiamento d’agricoltura, arti e manifatture, dell’Amministrazione delle Ferrovie e, nel Novecento, della scuola media Giuseppe Verga. Acquistato dall’Amministrazione Provinciale nel 1984 e successivamente restaurato, dal 2013 è affidato alla Fondazione Sant’Elia e aperto al pubblico come sede espositiva.

Una storia ancora più antica caratterizza il Loggiato di San Bartolomeo, in corso Vittorio Emanuele, a pochi passi da Porta Felice e affacciato sul Foro Italico. Il complesso era originariamente parte dell’Ospedale di San Bartolomeo, fondato nella prima metà del XIII secolo dall’omonima confraternita. Dei diversi corpi dell’antico ospedale, gravemente danneggiato dai bombardamenti del maggio 1943, sopravvisse proprio il loggiato seicentesco a due ordini, caratterizzato da archi a tutto sesto al livello inferiore e da aperture dal profilo sinuoso a quello superiore, concluso da una balaustra traforata.

Dopo i restauri, il Loggiato è stato riaperto al pubblico nel 1998 e ha progressivamente assunto una forte vocazione per l’arte contemporanea, ospitando mostre di artisti come Tano Festa, Renato Mambor, Emilio Greco, Giacomo Manzù, Pedro Cano, Croce Taravella, Giuseppe Modica, Piero Guccione, Gregorio Botta e Igor Mitoraj . Proprio Mitoraj ha lasciato davanti all’ala occidentale del complesso Eroe elimo , scultura monumentale in bronzo dedicata alla storia mediterranea della città.

Dal giugno 2025 il Loggiato è stato riconsegnato alla Città Metropolitana per un intervento di riqualificazione finanziato nell’ambito del PNRR e finalizzato soprattutto a migliorarne l’accessibilità.

title_original: 《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》：所有和語言相關的，都是我們鬥氣的理由
title_zh: 《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》：所有和語言相關的，都是我們鬥氣的理由
summary_zh: 来源摘录：《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》把時間交還給高中生，以他們為主體，用自己的聲音去訴說自己怎麼理解／感覺她的寫作。客觀而言，每個人閱讀小說的心得，充其量都只能代表自己。但是，假如我們認真分析千禧年後出生的這些法國高中生，他們閱讀安妮艾諾的心境──在著作出版三、四十年後的法國，安妮．艾諾對 Z 世代還有意義嗎？ 這篇文章 《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》：所有和語言相關的，都是我們鬥氣的理由 最早出現於 釀電影 。

"場景一。教室裡，女孩慢慢朗讀《記憶無非徹底看透的一切》。主角墮胎的段落：「我跑向走廊盡頭的廁所／蹲在馬桶上／面對著門／我看著雙腿間的磁磚／我使盡全身力氣推／那東西像手榴彈一樣炸開⋯⋯」在她身旁的兩個男孩，在座位上摀著嘴，坐立不安。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "場景二。另一所高中，女孩們課後熱烈討論《記憶無非徹底看透的一切》。女孩追問男孩：「你無法設身處地，去想想墮胎女性的感受嗎？」男孩十分錯愕，沒辦法回答。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "場景三。男孩說讀艾諾的書，讓他想起父母的秘密。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不分男女，有時他們會說：這本書讓他們想起父母。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "這些都是《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》（Writing Life – Annie Ernaux Through the Eyes of High School Students，2025）。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本片把時間交還給高中生，以他們為主體，用自己的聲音去訴說自己怎麼理解／感覺她的寫作。客觀而言，每個人閱讀小說的心得，充其量都只能代表自己。但是，假如我們再退一步，假如我們認真分析千禧年後出生的這些法國高中生，他們閱讀安妮艾諾的心境── 在著作出版三、四十年後的法國， 安妮．艾諾（Annie Ernaux） 寫的內容，還能震撼人心嗎？對 Z 世代還有意義嗎？", "links": "https://img.vocus.cc/B5TQ-CR_a2tpC5yNRoB_tNO8uDSEgbwC9ijU-s_JSG0/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/d9774b92-f021-412f-9622-f27285d975a9.png", "alt": "《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》電影劇照／劇照提供：IDFA Institute", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》電影劇照／劇照提供：IDFA Institute"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "02."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "經年捕捉社會第一手現場的紀錄片導演克萊兒．西蒙（Claire Simon），2023 年以《診間身景》（Notre corps）揭露醫療體制內，女性身體的微妙處境；2018 年則以《年輕的孤寂》（Premières solitudes）貼身記錄當代青年的內心風景；而 2016 年《電影夢的開始》（Le concours）則記述 La Fémis 巴黎高等國立電影學院入學考試，近千人耗時半年有餘的激烈選拔過程。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "克萊兒．西蒙在新作《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》依然深入教育現場，旁觀高中生激辯安妮．艾諾書中女性角色的「位置」，與艾諾如何依靠文化知識翻轉階級，以及她與家庭之間的扞格和衝突。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "攝影機靜置在教室中間，鏡頭直面學生談論的側臉。不同的老師將學生圍成一圈，事前分組讓他們讀完艾諾的書，問他們：安妮．艾諾為什麼這樣寫？你能不能朗讀一下她的文字？以及，讀完之後你想到甚麼？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "全片結構工整，風格日常純粹，一所高中接著一所高中，記錄學生們課堂中與下課後的討論，沒有為了戲劇化而製造時間的倒錯、敘事的匱缺，或過多浮想聯翩的留白。 宛如多張蓋玻片輪流放到顯微鏡下面，而同樣的問題引導，也將因為這些青少年出生於不同的家庭／成長背景，而讀出不同的重點。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "這部片的某種意在言外，若從導演的拍攝足跡切入，會是重要的一把鑰匙：《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》走訪的高中，分別橫跨多個城鎮，弗朗孔維爾（Franconville）、卡宴（Cayenne）、薩塞勒（Sarcelles）、索恩河畔自由城（Villefranche-sur-Saône）、土魯斯（Toulouse）、聖克里斯托爾－萊薩萊斯（Saint-Christol-lez-Alès）。從首都附近到海外的法屬圭亞那（Guyane française），地理位置的選定與跳接，在形式上似乎也圍繞著安妮．艾諾的其中一個寫作核心，即是語言與階級的鬆動。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/9DCHEj1dmEieIsaPS_M5OEeuF-NONb_CtqcwjckLzh4/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/45bd9ab5-de27-40b2-8067-074e234f9993.jpg", "alt": "《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "克萊兒．西蒙如何呈現這些高中生的閱讀差異？片中的重要刺點之一，是導演在卡宴的拍攝。卡宴位處法屬圭亞那，在歷史上長期被法國政府視為流放地。克萊兒．西蒙來此拍攝有其意義，如同她曾在法國媒體專訪的回應： 「我為什麼要去圭亞那？因為根本沒人去那裡。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在卡宴的斐利克斯埃布埃高中，一位女孩對安妮．艾諾寫作語言上的堅持格外敏感、認同。在法屬圭亞那，除了官方語言法語，還有多種語言並存，女孩說：「她成功地把一些細微的語句放進作品裡，來展現自己的出身。」讀安妮．艾諾的小說，讓她深深有感： 「有些人會說克里奧爾語（Creole）不是一個能用來談情說愛的語言；有人說用克里奧爾語討論愛，一點也不美。我認為這一點也不正確。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "老師沒有放過這個關於語言教育的機會。他讓另一個學生上臺，隨意寫下某個克里奧爾語的單詞，學生寫「mezammi」，老師問她要怎麼翻回法文，學生說：「我不會翻譯，我只知道怎麼解釋。」老師再問：「所以這是什麼意思呢？」學生再答：「你遇到事情，覺得很驚訝的時候，就可以用這個字。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "接著又換另一個學生上臺，寫下「Mwen enmen'w」，老師不解，於是嘗試正確發音，師生關係忽然倒錯，克里奧爾語變成短暫的主角，老師反而要虛心向學。老師問：「『Mwen enmen'w』又是什麼意思？」學生說：「這句是『我愛你』。」。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "課堂最後，喜歡克里奧爾語的女孩說：「其實我從未去過海地，但是我媽讓我泡在海地的文化跟語言中長大；在圭亞那，大家都熟悉克里奧爾語所唱的歌。」她無法準確講出諸如語言越位之類的定義，但已經在安妮．艾諾的小說中，讀到自己身處環境的某些蛛絲馬跡。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《位置》（La Place，1983）中的安妮．艾諾，回憶自己曾經強烈指責父親的法語發音不夠正確，不只影響她，也讓她感覺丟臉：「所有和語言相關的，在我記憶裡，都是我們鬥氣的理由、我們使性子的原因，這比錢的問題還嚴重。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "女孩也說，她在書裡讀到安妮．艾諾透過教育獲取知識，成為作家、老師，階級翻身，但她的父母還留在原地： 「我在她身上看到一點自己的影子。她的書讓我確認了一些事，讓我心想：原來我不是唯一一個。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一個女孩，則對這一切稍稍嗤之以鼻：「老師，我覺得我可以理解艾諾的心情。但我不認為她有什麼值得為自己的出身感到羞愧的。我覺得人要接受自己的背景，接受我們從何而來。」"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/AJhMqkUP51IfP0BpejQfQkrfpxU_FPCefJkXSR3_SAk/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/61749e83-8651-441d-83c7-5210f9ec4a13.png", "alt": "《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》電影劇照／劇照提供：IDFA Institute", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》電影劇照／劇照提供：IDFA Institute"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "03."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一組高中，克萊兒．西蒙來到南法的一座小城，聖克里斯托爾－萊薩萊斯。這一組高中生在讀完安妮．艾諾的小說時，紛紛想起自己生活裡小小的秘密──「譬如，我自己去藥局買了事後藥，我用自己的錢買，我當時沒帶健保卡，不然事後藥應該是免費的⋯⋯但這件事沒人知道，不然我覺得其實會有所幫助。」老師問她，是否跟父母聊過這件事，女孩搖頭：「我其實已經試過了。我覺得只一提到，他們就很不自在。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "也有女孩把艾諾的書作為療傷之書：「晚上或下午，我會打開書，在沙發上看⋯⋯就像是在替自己療傷。這件事連我也覺得很瘋狂，因為她（安妮．艾諾）語氣超冷。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "還有一群女孩課後等公車。此處閒談，成為本片最動人的橋段。一群女孩聚在一起，不再談論文本。但分享的生活細節，卻無不令人想起安妮．艾諾。 某一女孩為了參與派對，瞞著家人，翻身從房間跳窗而下，導致骨盆骨折，但還是要跟朋友去玩。她游泳，喝酒，回家後忍著創痛，母親得知後卻意外地沒有苛責，隔天女孩疼痛不止、無法走路，才意識到自己完蛋了。「對，我哭是因為，我終於意識到事情的嚴重性，我真的不知道在做什麼。但我媽從沒懲罰我。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "安妮．艾諾的書在數十年後，以一種非常幽微的形式，鑽進這些年輕讀者的內心──那些慾望的奔騰、對世界規則的掙脫、自我誠實的追求，女孩覺得痛快，撕開世界的假面；男孩覺得抑鬱、困惑，原來有些傷，從頭開始他們就認不得，驚嘆竟有這種「拒絕優雅」的寫作。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "曾有男孩回覆，他覺得這些令他震驚的內容，基本上與他無關。但是小說所寫的，未必只存在於小說之中："}, {"type": "quote", "text": "「我的人生，也許只有唯一一個目標：將我的身體、感覺、想法化作文字，也就是某種清楚易懂、普遍性的東西，好讓我的生命完完全全融進其他人的腦海與生活。」──《記憶無非徹底看透的一切》（L'Événement，2000）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "鏡頭的最後，只剩下一個女孩還沒搭上公車。克萊兒．西蒙問她，妳也寫作嗎？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "女孩有些怯生生地說，寫一點點。她回憶 2017 年，在筆記本上寫到自己想成為作家，覺得成為真正的作家，就一定要分享個人經歷和群體經歷⋯⋯"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "克萊兒．西蒙笑著說：「我覺得妳好像在講安妮．艾諾喔。」女孩有點害羞，說，是沒錯。但家裡的人很討厭安妮．艾諾的書，這常讓她覺得，自己是不是做錯了什麼。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "導演問：「那麼，妳現在心裡怎麼想？」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "女孩離開前，堅定地看著鏡頭：「我要聽我心底的聲音，我覺得一定要閱讀。」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "（完）"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/_JA0JF8_h49wIbRVNXxddvHd2oFeNbCXWfc_1moiKzs/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/4914b333-86ef-46b2-a52b-69ec541173d3.jpg", "alt": "《釀電影》女人沒有鄉愁──𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 台灣國際女性影展專題／圖像提供：釀電影", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《釀電影》女人沒有鄉愁──𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 台灣國際女性影展專題／圖像提供：釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "將於 2026 年 10 月 16 日正式開展的第 33 屆女性影展，以「非分擾動 Into the Drift」為年度視覺，藉由流動、穿梭的視覺意象，向當代持續變動的疆界、關係發出提問，嘗試在一個世紀的電影裡，尋找錨定自身位置，重新想像自由的樣貌。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《釀電影》編輯室以 「女人沒有鄉愁」 為策展專題，延伸「流動」一詞作為觀看當代世界的方法，循著穿行於城市與鄉野、家庭與個體、戰爭與和平之間的選擇，即從無法無家、無法有家，又何處不是家的概念出發，嘗試看見女性在巨大歷史的移動軌跡之中，曾經被隱匿、邊緣的流離。", "links": [{"text": "「女人沒有鄉愁」", "url": "https://filmaholic.tw/covers/2026wmw/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "當「鄉愁」經常性地被放置在傳統父權結構底下，指涉國族敘事框架、血緣根源、既定秩序的眷戀與歸返，自破除疆界而起的遊牧，便關乎於女性電影中的身分、身體、時間與抗爭之路徑。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本次專題委邀策展人陳慧穎進行訪問，自「屬於她的遊蕩」單元的六部電影作品展開，重新爬梳半世紀的世界之變，與存於其中的不變；同時亦邀請獨立評論人陳穎，深入分析「屬於她的遊蕩」單元中，三部來自八〇、九〇年代的導演首作，以「移動」與「身體性」為軸，試論空間為性別運動、女性主義所開創的嶄新變革。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "圍繞著「跨越」、「移動」的概念，今年的「焦點影人」單元為非裔法國電影導演莎拉・馬羅多羅（Sarah Maldoror，1929－2020），本次也將收錄獨立評論人黃曦，自多部經典電影爬梳女性主義與反殖民運動、去殖民途徑的抵抗力量。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "延續關於時間、時代之思索，本專題另有三篇獨立評論，分別由獨立評論人許騰云、小說家趙鴻祐與新銳評論人黎思行執筆。透過普拉迪・克里申（Pradip Krishen）《安尼閣來舞這齣》（In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones，1989）回到七〇年代，與作家阿蘭達蒂・洛伊（Arundhati Roy）進行跨越世代對話；接著隨克萊兒・西蒙（Claire Simon）《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》（Writing Life – Annie Ernaux Through the Eyes of High School Students，2025）與當代學子的對讀，將書寫轉化為面向未來、身分的路徑；最後由琳恩・薩克斯（Lynne Sachs）《相遇皆有痕》（Every Contact Leaves a Trace，2025）的實驗性展開評析，記述散文電影無有時間，卻凝刻空間、記憶的痕跡。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最後，本專題亦與《沒有的派對》（Sometimes, I Imagine Them All at a Party，2026）導演丹妮亞拉・麥蘭妮・胡勒（Daniela Melanie Goode）展開深入對談，自導演十餘年後執起攝影機，透過多重影像媒介將創傷記憶轉化為與公共對話，甚至對抗體制的政治力量，以期提出一種嶄新的、當代的對話空間是──「女人沒有鄉愁」的起點不在故土，而在踏出疆界、凝視創傷、重構語言與時間的游蕩中，我們如何在生命的蜿蜒之中，持續闖蕩？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "✹「女人沒有鄉愁」專題閱讀情由此 ✹", article_text:
撰文／趙鴻祐 劇照提供／台灣國際女性影展 責任編輯／黃曦 核稿編輯／黃曦

01.

場景一。教室裡，女孩慢慢朗讀《記憶無非徹底看透的一切》。主角墮胎的段落：「我跑向走廊盡頭的廁所／蹲在馬桶上／面對著門／我看著雙腿間的磁磚／我使盡全身力氣推／那東西像手榴彈一樣炸開⋯⋯」在她身旁的兩個男孩，在座位上摀著嘴，坐立不安。

場景二。另一所高中，女孩們課後熱烈討論《記憶無非徹底看透的一切》。女孩追問男孩：「你無法設身處地，去想想墮胎女性的感受嗎？」男孩十分錯愕，沒辦法回答。

場景三。男孩說讀艾諾的書，讓他想起父母的秘密。

不分男女，有時他們會說：這本書讓他們想起父母。

這些都是《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》（Writing Life – Annie Ernaux Through the Eyes of High School Students，2025）。

本片把時間交還給高中生，以他們為主體，用自己的聲音去訴說自己怎麼理解／感覺她的寫作。客觀而言，每個人閱讀小說的心得，充其量都只能代表自己。但是，假如我們再退一步，假如我們認真分析千禧年後出生的這些法國高中生，他們閱讀安妮艾諾的心境── 在著作出版三、四十年後的法國， 安妮．艾諾（Annie Ernaux） 寫的內容，還能震撼人心嗎？對 Z 世代還有意義嗎？

《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》電影劇照／劇照提供：IDFA Institute

02.

經年捕捉社會第一手現場的紀錄片導演克萊兒．西蒙（Claire Simon），2023 年以《診間身景》（Notre corps）揭露醫療體制內，女性身體的微妙處境；2018 年則以《年輕的孤寂》（Premières solitudes）貼身記錄當代青年的內心風景；而 2016 年《電影夢的開始》（Le concours）則記述 La Fémis 巴黎高等國立電影學院入學考試，近千人耗時半年有餘的激烈選拔過程。

克萊兒．西蒙在新作《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》依然深入教育現場，旁觀高中生激辯安妮．艾諾書中女性角色的「位置」，與艾諾如何依靠文化知識翻轉階級，以及她與家庭之間的扞格和衝突。

攝影機靜置在教室中間，鏡頭直面學生談論的側臉。不同的老師將學生圍成一圈，事前分組讓他們讀完艾諾的書，問他們：安妮．艾諾為什麼這樣寫？你能不能朗讀一下她的文字？以及，讀完之後你想到甚麼？

全片結構工整，風格日常純粹，一所高中接著一所高中，記錄學生們課堂中與下課後的討論，沒有為了戲劇化而製造時間的倒錯、敘事的匱缺，或過多浮想聯翩的留白。 宛如多張蓋玻片輪流放到顯微鏡下面，而同樣的問題引導，也將因為這些青少年出生於不同的家庭／成長背景，而讀出不同的重點。

這部片的某種意在言外，若從導演的拍攝足跡切入，會是重要的一把鑰匙：《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》走訪的高中，分別橫跨多個城鎮，弗朗孔維爾（Franconville）、卡宴（Cayenne）、薩塞勒（Sarcelles）、索恩河畔自由城（Villefranche-sur-Saône）、土魯斯（Toulouse）、聖克里斯托爾－萊薩萊斯（Saint-Christol-lez-Alès）。從首都附近到海外的法屬圭亞那（Guyane française），地理位置的選定與跳接，在形式上似乎也圍繞著安妮．艾諾的其中一個寫作核心，即是語言與階級的鬆動。

《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》電影劇照／劇照提供：台灣國際女性影展

克萊兒．西蒙如何呈現這些高中生的閱讀差異？片中的重要刺點之一，是導演在卡宴的拍攝。卡宴位處法屬圭亞那，在歷史上長期被法國政府視為流放地。克萊兒．西蒙來此拍攝有其意義，如同她曾在法國媒體專訪的回應： 「我為什麼要去圭亞那？因為根本沒人去那裡。」

在卡宴的斐利克斯埃布埃高中，一位女孩對安妮．艾諾寫作語言上的堅持格外敏感、認同。在法屬圭亞那，除了官方語言法語，還有多種語言並存，女孩說：「她成功地把一些細微的語句放進作品裡，來展現自己的出身。」讀安妮．艾諾的小說，讓她深深有感： 「有些人會說克里奧爾語（Creole）不是一個能用來談情說愛的語言；有人說用克里奧爾語討論愛，一點也不美。我認為這一點也不正確。」

老師沒有放過這個關於語言教育的機會。他讓另一個學生上臺，隨意寫下某個克里奧爾語的單詞，學生寫「mezammi」，老師問她要怎麼翻回法文，學生說：「我不會翻譯，我只知道怎麼解釋。」老師再問：「所以這是什麼意思呢？」學生再答：「你遇到事情，覺得很驚訝的時候，就可以用這個字。」

接著又換另一個學生上臺，寫下「Mwen enmen'w」，老師不解，於是嘗試正確發音，師生關係忽然倒錯，克里奧爾語變成短暫的主角，老師反而要虛心向學。老師問：「『Mwen enmen'w』又是什麼意思？」學生說：「這句是『我愛你』。」。

課堂最後，喜歡克里奧爾語的女孩說：「其實我從未去過海地，但是我媽讓我泡在海地的文化跟語言中長大；在圭亞那，大家都熟悉克里奧爾語所唱的歌。」她無法準確講出諸如語言越位之類的定義，但已經在安妮．艾諾的小說中，讀到自己身處環境的某些蛛絲馬跡。

《位置》（La Place，1983）中的安妮．艾諾，回憶自己曾經強烈指責父親的法語發音不夠正確，不只影響她，也讓她感覺丟臉：「所有和語言相關的，在我記憶裡，都是我們鬥氣的理由、我們使性子的原因，這比錢的問題還嚴重。」

女孩也說，她在書裡讀到安妮．艾諾透過教育獲取知識，成為作家、老師，階級翻身，但她的父母還留在原地： 「我在她身上看到一點自己的影子。她的書讓我確認了一些事，讓我心想：原來我不是唯一一個。」

另一個女孩，則對這一切稍稍嗤之以鼻：「老師，我覺得我可以理解艾諾的心情。但我不認為她有什麼值得為自己的出身感到羞愧的。我覺得人要接受自己的背景，接受我們從何而來。」

《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》電影劇照／劇照提供：IDFA Institute

03.

另一組高中，克萊兒．西蒙來到南法的一座小城，聖克里斯托爾－萊薩萊斯。這一組高中生在讀完安妮．艾諾的小說時，紛紛想起自己生活裡小小的秘密──「譬如，我自己去藥局買了事後藥，我用自己的錢買，我當時沒帶健保卡，不然事後藥應該是免費的⋯⋯但這件事沒人知道，不然我覺得其實會有所幫助。」老師問她，是否跟父母聊過這件事，女孩搖頭：「我其實已經試過了。我覺得只一提到，他們就很不自在。」

也有女孩把艾諾的書作為療傷之書：「晚上或下午，我會打開書，在沙發上看⋯⋯就像是在替自己療傷。這件事連我也覺得很瘋狂，因為她（安妮．艾諾）語氣超冷。」

還有一群女孩課後等公車。此處閒談，成為本片最動人的橋段。一群女孩聚在一起，不再談論文本。但分享的生活細節，卻無不令人想起安妮．艾諾。 某一女孩為了參與派對，瞞著家人，翻身從房間跳窗而下，導致骨盆骨折，但還是要跟朋友去玩。她游泳，喝酒，回家後忍著創痛，母親得知後卻意外地沒有苛責，隔天女孩疼痛不止、無法走路，才意識到自己完蛋了。「對，我哭是因為，我終於意識到事情的嚴重性，我真的不知道在做什麼。但我媽從沒懲罰我。」

安妮．艾諾的書在數十年後，以一種非常幽微的形式，鑽進這些年輕讀者的內心──那些慾望的奔騰、對世界規則的掙脫、自我誠實的追求，女孩覺得痛快，撕開世界的假面；男孩覺得抑鬱、困惑，原來有些傷，從頭開始他們就認不得，驚嘆竟有這種「拒絕優雅」的寫作。

曾有男孩回覆，他覺得這些令他震驚的內容，基本上與他無關。但是小說所寫的，未必只存在於小說之中：

「我的人生，也許只有唯一一個目標：將我的身體、感覺、想法化作文字，也就是某種清楚易懂、普遍性的東西，好讓我的生命完完全全融進其他人的腦海與生活。」──《記憶無非徹底看透的一切》（L'Événement，2000）

鏡頭的最後，只剩下一個女孩還沒搭上公車。克萊兒．西蒙問她，妳也寫作嗎？

女孩有些怯生生地說，寫一點點。她回憶 2017 年，在筆記本上寫到自己想成為作家，覺得成為真正的作家，就一定要分享個人經歷和群體經歷⋯⋯

克萊兒．西蒙笑著說：「我覺得妳好像在講安妮．艾諾喔。」女孩有點害羞，說，是沒錯。但家裡的人很討厭安妮．艾諾的書，這常讓她覺得，自己是不是做錯了什麼。

導演問：「那麼，妳現在心裡怎麼想？」

女孩離開前，堅定地看著鏡頭：「我要聽我心底的聲音，我覺得一定要閱讀。」

（完）

《釀電影》女人沒有鄉愁──𝟤𝟢𝟤𝟨 台灣國際女性影展專題／圖像提供：釀電影

將於 2026 年 10 月 16 日正式開展的第 33 屆女性影展，以「非分擾動 Into the Drift」為年度視覺，藉由流動、穿梭的視覺意象，向當代持續變動的疆界、關係發出提問，嘗試在一個世紀的電影裡，尋找錨定自身位置，重新想像自由的樣貌。

《釀電影》編輯室以 「女人沒有鄉愁」 為策展專題，延伸「流動」一詞作為觀看當代世界的方法，循著穿行於城市與鄉野、家庭與個體、戰爭與和平之間的選擇，即從無法無家、無法有家，又何處不是家的概念出發，嘗試看見女性在巨大歷史的移動軌跡之中，曾經被隱匿、邊緣的流離。

當「鄉愁」經常性地被放置在傳統父權結構底下，指涉國族敘事框架、血緣根源、既定秩序的眷戀與歸返，自破除疆界而起的遊牧，便關乎於女性電影中的身分、身體、時間與抗爭之路徑。

本次專題委邀策展人陳慧穎進行訪問，自「屬於她的遊蕩」單元的六部電影作品展開，重新爬梳半世紀的世界之變，與存於其中的不變；同時亦邀請獨立評論人陳穎，深入分析「屬於她的遊蕩」單元中，三部來自八〇、九〇年代的導演首作，以「移動」與「身體性」為軸，試論空間為性別運動、女性主義所開創的嶄新變革。

圍繞著「跨越」、「移動」的概念，今年的「焦點影人」單元為非裔法國電影導演莎拉・馬羅多羅（Sarah Maldoror，1929－2020），本次也將收錄獨立評論人黃曦，自多部經典電影爬梳女性主義與反殖民運動、去殖民途徑的抵抗力量。

延續關於時間、時代之思索，本專題另有三篇獨立評論，分別由獨立評論人許騰云、小說家趙鴻祐與新銳評論人黎思行執筆。透過普拉迪・克里申（Pradip Krishen）《安尼閣來舞這齣》（In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones，1989）回到七〇年代，與作家阿蘭達蒂・洛伊（Arundhati Roy）進行跨越世代對話；接著隨克萊兒・西蒙（Claire Simon）《我們的青春與安妮艾諾》（Writing Life – Annie Ernaux Through the Eyes of High School Students，2025）與當代學子的對讀，將書寫轉化為面向未來、身分的路徑；最後由琳恩・薩克斯（Lynne Sachs）《相遇皆有痕》（Every Contact Leaves a Trace，2025）的實驗性展開評析，記述散文電影無有時間，卻凝刻空間、記憶的痕跡。

最後，本專題亦與《沒有的派對》（Sometimes, I Imagine Them All at a Party，2026）導演丹妮亞拉・麥蘭妮・胡勒（Daniela Melanie Goode）展開深入對談，自導演十餘年後執起攝影機，透過多重影像媒介將創傷記憶轉化為與公共對話，甚至對抗體制的政治力量，以期提出一種嶄新的、當代的對話空間是──「女人沒有鄉愁」的起點不在故土，而在踏出疆界、凝視創傷、重構語言與時間的游蕩中，我們如何在生命的蜿蜒之中，持續闖蕩？

article_text:
葛飾応為「吉原格子先之図」 夜景の系譜

会場：太田記念美術館（東京都渋谷区神宮前１－１０－１０）

会期：２０２６年１０月６日（火）～１２月６日（日）

休館日：休館日は１０月１３、１９、２６日。１１月２、４～６、９、１６、２４、３０日

開館時間：１０：３０～１７：３０（入館は１７：００まで）

アクセス：ＪＲ山手線原宿駅から徒歩５分、東京メトロ千代田線・副都心線明治神宮前駅から徒歩３分

観覧料：一般１２００円、高校生・大学生８００円、中学生以下無料

※所蔵の記載がない作品はすべて太田記念美術館蔵 ※前期（～１１月３日）、後期（１１月７日～）で「吉原格子先之図」以外、全点展示替え

※最新情報は、 公式ＨＰ で確認を。問い合わせはハローダイヤル（０５０－５５４１－８６００）へ。

浮世絵を専門に収集・展示する太田記念美術館の「看板」のひとつとなっているのが、葛飾応為の「吉原格子先之図」である。世界でもっとも有名な浮世絵師・葛飾北斎の娘である応為は、現存する肉筆画が世界で10点あまり、ゲームの世界でいう「レアキャラ」みたいな存在だが、中でもこの「吉原格子先之図」は夜の遊郭、光と闇の描き方が秀逸で、高い人気を誇る作品なのである。３年ぶりの同作品公開となる今回の展覧会は、この作品にちなんで浮世絵における「夜景」がテーマ。鈴木春信や歌川広重、小林清親といった浮世絵史を彩った名手たちの、「夜」を描いた作品をずらり並べた展示である。

「吉原格子先之図」の展示で幕を開ける展覧会は以降、〈江戸の夜景Ⅰ 青の夜空・黒の夜空〉〈江戸の夜景Ⅱ 濃紺の夜空〉〈闇夜物語－戦い・事件・伝説－〉〈明治の夜景〉〈日本土産としての夜景〉の５ブロックに分かれている。

浮世絵における「夜」の描写のターニングポイントとなったのが、「ベロ藍」といわれる濃紺の絵具の導入。「プルシアンブルー」といわれるこの合成顔料は、18世紀初頭にドイツ・ベルリンで発見され、日本には18世紀中葉に紹介された。1820年代後半に大量に輸入されるようになり、北斎や広重ら多くの絵師が愛用するようになった。〈江戸の夜景Ⅰ 青の夜空・黒の夜空〉は、その「ベロ藍」が普及する前、絵師たちがどのように夜空を表現していたかに注目。〈江戸の夜景Ⅱ 濃紺の夜空〉は、「ベロ藍」を特に効果的に使った広重の作品を中心に展示している。

それに続く〈闇夜物語－戦い・事件・伝説－〉は、夜にまつわる様々な物語や伝説、歴史的な事件・戦闘を描いた作品を特集。「曽我の仇討」や「忠臣蔵」など、夜に展開する物語は昔から多い。さらにいえば、妖怪・幽霊の数々は、夜の世界を主な活躍の場にしていたりする。だからこそ、浮世絵の世界でも長年、人々に愛されてきた作品が多いのである。月光の下で繰り広げられる物語の数々を描写した月岡芳年の連作「月百姿」は一例だろうか。「累伝説」を描いた歌川国芳の「木曽街道六十九次之内 鵜沼 与右エ門 女房累」、夫の敵討ちを果たした女盗賊を描く落合芳幾「英名二十八衆句 鬼神於松」など、見どころたっぷり。

〈明治の夜景〉で中心となるのが。浮世絵に西洋画の技法を持ち込んだ小林清親。ビビッドな光と影の描写が評判をとり、その作品は「光線画」と呼ばれた。「両国花火之図」は、その特徴が如実に表れているものだ。清親が「光線画」を手掛けた時期は比較的身近かったが、弟子の井上安治だけでなく、下に挙げた「湯島之景」の小倉柳村や鈴木年基らがフォロワーとして登場した。そして、それは明治30年代に浮世絵が衰退していった後も、日本の木版画に影響を与え続けたのである。

浮世絵衰退後、明治末から大正期にかけて、多くの「輸出用版画」が制作されるようになるのだが、そこでは「夜の風景」が描かれることも多かった。それらの作品をまとめて紹介しているのが、最後のブロック〈日本土産としての夜景〉。上に挙げた「A High Bridge by Night」は、展覧会図録によると、清親だけでなくアメリカとイギリスで活躍した画家ジェームズ・マクニール・ホイッスラーの「ノクターン―青と金、オールド・バターシー・ブリッジ」の影響もみられるという。「輸出用版画」は「浮世絵」と「新版画」をつなぐ存在として、最近注目されつつあるが、まだまだ十分に研究されているとはいえないジャンル。その作品が美術ファンの目に触れる、めったにない機会だともいえる。江戸から明治、大正まで、浮世絵とそれに続く木版画の夜の表現を網羅した今回の展覧会、そういう意味でも価値があるといえるのである。（美術展ナビ取材班 田中聡）

article_text:
After a busy year that’s seen the Canal+ Group complete a wave of acquisitions across two continents, Anna Marsh , the CEO of Studiocanal and the deputy CEO and chief content officer for Canal+, insisted such moves have been instrumental in strengthening the position of the French media giant at a time of unprecedented industry disruption.

“It’s really important to have a fresh perspective. People that are going to challenge the status quo. Because the business is moving so fast,” said the New Zealand-born exec, who appeared in conversation at Rome’s MIA Market on Wednesday with MIA head Gaia Tridente.

Related Stories

Elizabeth Holmes Mania: 'You Can See Everything' Drives 186% Viewership Spike for Amanda Seyfried's 'The Dropout' (EXCLUSIVE)

‘You Can See Everything’ Sets Oscar Campaigns for Best Picture, Supporting Actress and More Categories

“The audience is so tough that we constantly need to be looking at ourselves in the mirror. AI is emerging right now. We’ve got enormous consolidation in the U.S. Looking at the different ways that the borders between pay TV and free TV are colliding,” Marsh continued.

“There are so many questions to ask. Nobody has all the answers. When we’re able to expand, when we’re able to acquire new companies and enter into new territories, it’s truly enriching.”

Marsh was speaking in Rome on the heels of GREENLit, MIA’s flagship drama showcase, which offered an exclusive first look at four upcoming international series, among them “Gucci: Game Over,” a six-episode miniseries based on Allegra Gucci’s memoir that’s co-produced by Sky Studios and Lucky Red and distributed internationally by Studiocanal.

Marsh praised the series as a testament to “the culture, the courage, the history that Europe’s been blessed with,” while insisting to the assembled industry professionals in the room, “I think Europe has a great future when it comes to storytelling. And the depth of the stories that we can tell here is absolutely endless.”

The Canal+ Group acquired a majority stake in Lucky Red, the Rome-based distribution and production company, in February. It was the latest in a series of moves made by the French media conglomerate to expand its growing footprint. Earlier this year, the group acquired a 34-percent stake in UGC, the Paris-headquartered film studio that operates one of France’s leading cinema chains, and also completed a $2 billion takeover of South African pay-TV company MultiChoice.

That move helped to boost the Canal+ subscriber base to north of 40 million, more than half of whom are English-speaking, thanks to MultiChoice’s reach across the African continent.

“That just opens a wealth of opportunity,” said Marsh, who touted recent Canal+ and Studiocanal projects like “The Road Home,” an apartheid-era drama starring Cynthia Erivo, Thabo Rametsi and Guy Pearce which recently wrapped shooting in South Africa, and “Shadow Has Fallen,” a Canal+ original action series, whose third season wrapped in Cape Town.

“That’s a really strategic part of the group’s focus right now,” she said, of the company’s Africa expansion. “And you can really see how Studiocanal is at the heart of that strategy. If we, as Canal+, enter a new market with so much potential as South Africa, we have to have a strong content strategy.”

Another pillar in that strategy is Studiocanal Stories, a specialty label launched in 2024 that’s dedicated to book adaptations. Pointing to the blockbuster “ Paddington ” franchise as the company’s “biggest, most successful IP” to date — and one that “started as a book,” as she noted — Marsh stressed how optioning existing IP “allows us to relax a little bit” because it comes with a built-in audience.

“It does give confidence,” she said, “and it does allow us to put more money and more data behind the decision-making.”

Of course, when it comes to decision-making, some of the old metrics still apply — chief among them talent. That was certainly the case with “What Happens at Night,” an upcoming psychological horror adapted from Peter Cameron’s 2020 novel that’s produced by Apple Studios in partnership with Studiocanal.

Directed by Martin Scorsese — “one of the greatest cineastes of all time,” according to Marsh — and starring Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence, Marsh said the film is as close as one can get in these uncertain times to what she described as “a bit of a slam dunk.”

Still, nothing is guaranteed, with Marsh admitting, “It is harder and harder to hit the bull’s eye.” “Audiences are becoming more and more difficult and their standards are constantly raising,” she said. Especially with Gen Z audiences, “there’s just no room for error.”

The 12th edition of Rome’s MIA Market runs Oct. 19 – 23.

article_text:
美術館が好きすぎてついに大学に入り直して学芸員資格を勉強中の画家こにしななめさんが、主に関西で開催される美術展や展覧会をイラストと漫画で紹介するシリーズ「ななめ歩きの美術館」です。 今回は京都国立博物館で11月29日まで開催されている特別展「源氏物語 王朝のかがやき」をレポートします。

（画家・こにしななめ）

特別展「源氏物語 王朝のかがやき」京都会場

会場：京都国立博物館 平成知新館（京都府京都市東山区茶屋町527）

会期：2026年10月6日（火）～11月29日（日） 主な展示替 前期：10月6日（火）～11月1日（日）／ 後期：11月3日（火・祝）～11月29日（日） ※会期中、一部の作品は上記以外にも展示替を行います。

開館時間：9:00～17:30（入館は17:00まで）、金曜日は9:00～20:00（入館は19:30まで）

休館日：月曜日、11月24日（火） ※ただし、11月23日（月・祝）は開館

観覧料：一般2,200円 / 大学生1,200円 / 高校生700円

article_text:
The gusts forecast for opening weekend are pushing seventy-five miles an hour. Camille Binelli, who runs the festival’s photography department, is unruffled: “On the beach, it’ll hold.” Philippe Augier — the mayor of Deauville and president of Les Franciscaines, the cultural center that houses most of the exhibitions — is no more impressed. “This town has been married to photography since the day it was born,” he says.

The marriage has had its memorable episodes. In August 1951, Robert Capa set his trunks down on the boardwalk on assignment for Holiday , the American travel magazine, which was, in effect, footing the bill for his vacation. “He spent two months here,” the mayor notes, “and the women of Deauville never got over it, the party was that hot.”

That same summer, Magnum’s co-founder set in motion one of the agency’s first great collective undertakings. Eleven photographers, Henri Cartier-Bresson and Eve Arnold among them, divided up fourteen countries across five continents. Armed with a single questionnaire, they asked twenty- to twenty-five-year-olds about their daily lives, their dreams and their fears. Do you have a telephone at home? What do you think of the United Nations? How many children do you want?

“Generation X, as in the unknown generation, the one that came after the war,” explains Lionel Charrier, photo editor at Libération , who co-directs the festival with Jonas Tebib. The series ran in France in December 1952, in the magazine Point de vue, Images du monde . It resurfaces now in Deauville, flanked by two contemporary answers to it on Generation Z, in a room called — you could not make this up — Le Point de Vue.

One of those answers, “Country-Side,” comes from Bruce Gilden, a fixture of American street photography and a Magnum member since 1998. The photographer, who turned eighty the day before the opening, put hundreds of miles of Normandy farmland behind him, stopping at farms, agricultural fairs and one village fête to meet apprentices, students and farmers’ children between thirteen and thirty.

Down on the sand, the thirty-nine outsize prints of his New York retrospective add up to what Charrier calls “one of the largest exhibitions of the American photographer’s work in France.” “It was pretty funny, putting all that seventies New York fauna out on this beach,” he says, standing in front of the flash-lit portraits, where the grotesque surfaces with tenderness. The book that came out of those pictures, Coney Island , has been out of print for years. “Everybody fights over that book, and here you have it, on the beach, supersized.”

The other Magnum commission takes us out to the Cotentin. Cristina de Middel — who chaired the agency from 2022 to 2025 and has built her whole body of work on the porous border between documentary and fiction — settled in one of the most heavily nuclearized territories on the planet, where the “Aval du futur” program, announced in March 2024, promises the largest industrial project in the world. Residents learned about it from the press. To photograph the young people there, in “Les Atomiques de Cherbourg,” she went looking for the sets of The Umbrellas of Cherbourg : the station, the platform, Jacques Demy’s saturated color.

Back in Deauville, facing the sea, stand Tina Merandon’s arresting portraits of dogs and their owners; she holds a grant from the photo4food foundation. The French photographer has spent a decade on the bond between humans and animals. “Soudain la mêlée” catches the scrum itself, fur against skin. “A pack is a little frightening, and at the same time it’s very powerful,” she says. “I like it when things are moving all the time.” The hang melts into the landscape so completely that you lose track of where it stops: past the last frame, dogs off the leash are barreling down the sand.

At Les Franciscaines, the family drawers come open. Newsha Tavakolian, the Iranian photographer and Magnum member, has been photographing her country since she was sixteen. Her off-site residency was to be devoted to the young people of Tehran, and then the war broke out. Worried for her, Charrier offered her a way out. “She told me: no, no, I really want to document my country.” What she brought instead was forty-six glass plates inherited from a distant Kurdish great-uncle, and then her grandfather’s photographs. He had to give up the trade because his wife’s family was ashamed to see him walking around with a camera around his neck. Three generations of intimate images, her own among them, tell Iran’s transformations in the negative.

In the same space, Alain Keler, eighty-one — one of only two Frenchmen ever to win the W. Eugene Smith Grant — shows across from his son Léo, of the Hors-Format agency. “Souvenirs d’Honfleur” lines up the exhibits from a youth misspent between 1961 and 1964: jukeboxes, pinball machines, foosball tables, night buses, clandestine dashes to the nightclubs of Deauville. “It was an absolute madhouse. I came into my own,” he says, delighted. Sixty years later, he photographed a girl from his class picture at the door of their old lycée. Léo, for his part, collected the cahiers de doléances — the books of grievances drawn up during the Great National Debate of 2019 — and tracked down the Normans who had filled them with their lives, sometimes tragic, and their hopes, often disappointed.

Of the four winners of the Young Photographic Creation Prize, hung in with their elders, Flore Prébay asked family caregivers what they would do with a moment entirely their own. One of them answered: “Me, I’m going under. I can’t take any more.” Her portrait was taken at the bottom of a swimming pool.

Farther on, a wall goes to 100 Years , by the German artist Hans-Peter Feldmann, who died in 2023. On loan from the Musée d’Art Moderne de Paris, it presents a hundred and one portraits of strangers, from infant to centenarian. It is impossible not to place yourself somewhere on that frieze. “You arrive at your own age and you always find the person too old,” Jonas Tebib says.

On one side of the wall, the years already lived. On the other, the co-artistic director adds, “you can take the measure of the ones you have left.” Visitors have until January 3 to do the math.

“Generations,” the 17th edition of the Planches Contact Festival is on view in Deauville (France) through January 3, 2027.

article_text:
Through next February, New York’s Poster House is home to “Designed to Be Red,” a milestone survey of Native graphic arts. By institutional convention, such a show would unfold chronologically; but as its curator, the Native designer Brian Johnson, notes, time is a snake swallowing its own tail.

The show spans two centuries and more than 60 tribes and nations, organized around five themes: Indigenous Joy, Creative Sovereignty, Protest, It’s Complicated, and Extractive Marketing. The sections wrap around a single gallery, allowing visitors to begin at either end. It’s best to start from Joy, according to Johnson, though even that section’s psychedelic centerpieces—the ‘60s youthquake swept Native land, spectacularly—suggest trouble.

“Protest is literally the backbone of the entire gallery,” said Johnson, who is a citizen of the Monacan Indian Nation. Johnson assembled this show in part to correct the graphics arts record, which has both marginalized Native practitioners in its annals and left a legacy wound in the popular imagination. Americans surely remember the advertisements and have seen the movies: the heartbroken ‘Chief’, provocative princess, and proud warrior, infantilized by pidgin and hollowed of individuality.

“The whole idea behind this is multiplicity,” Johnson, who goes by he/they pronouns, said. “Native Americans and Indigenous peoples are not a single blanket. We are allowed to talk about ourselves and have ourselves seen, not as have a myth pushed onto us or woven into the American fabric.”

Among the participating artists are Kent Monkman, Onaman Collective (represented in the original posters they created for Dakota Access Pipeline protests); Anna Tsouhlarakis, who featured in the latest Whitney Biennial, contributed a banner from her Native Guide Project , that reads with the authority of Helvetica Bold: I Really Like the Way You Respect Native American Rights. The show, however, expands the notion of graphic arts beyond the boundaries drawn even by its host, Poster House. Jeffrey Gibson, who also appears in a series of jubilant collaborations with artists including Luzene Hill,Eric-Paul Riege, and Dana Claxton, is represented by a miniature ziggurat titled Because Once You Enter My House, It Becomes Our House (2020), and modeled after architecture of Cahokia, an ancient Native metropolis near modern St. Louis.

Craft, visual art, design: Where does Tony Gonyea’s ceramic wampum belt, which draws on a Haudenosaunee tradition dating to the mid-16th century, fall? And what of Ella Myers’s shadow box, Navajo Dye Chart , which, as its name suggests, displays some 40 plants and the colors they produce on wool?

“There’s a wall that is assumed, or imposed, between these categories, but someone can be a basket weaver or a rug weaver and also be engaged in graphic design. Art and design meld into everything,” Johnson said.

Read on for a conversation between Johnson and ARTnews on the show’s beginning, end, and next destination.

So, the title.

I love that the title is a double entendre: “Red” and “read.” I’m taking a racial slur and putting it right in your face, but the work is also designed to be read, understood, processed and contemplated. It’s like the Red Power movement or the American Indian Movement—taking something back that was very sacred to us and opening the entire show by punching it out.

It’s unusual to see so many three-dimensional objects in a graphic design show. What’s the thinking here?

One of the questions running through the exhibition is what counts as a poster.

For me, a poster, in a Native context, is something that communicates a message through typography, visual language or vernacular language, and is intended to be publicly shown or expressed.

Navajo Dye Chart shows how plants can be used to make different colors. The artist made posters in the 1980s, but the printing was on acidic paper and the work deteriorated quickly. There are letters still around, but I wanted the original chart—the actual object that shows where to find a particular plant and how it can be used to make a color.

That’s sovereignty: saying ‘these are the things you should be talking about.’ We don’t teach this in design history classes.

What do you make of that gap in arts and design education?

In school, we’re told that the Germans did everything, that design began with the Bauhaus, that this is how it has to be: Swiss typography. After the Bauhaus, people came to Yale, taught at Black Mountain College, and then those ideas disseminated to Cranbrook, Otis, CalArts, and other schools. Art education is stuck in the deep shadow of the Bauhaus.

[I’m a partner] at Polymode . We’ve been designing books and museum show for 20 years. In 2020, we started a school BIPOC Design History . We look at people of color who have been deliberately erased and left out of the design canon. Our school offers classes about Black design in America, Diseño Gráfico, a SWANA course, “(re)Creating Turtle Island”—we ask designers and researchers to show us what they think has been left out.

The section “Alcatraz and Protest” further complicates the distinctions between art, object, and design.

In 1969, Native Americans occupied Alcatraz Island, off San Francisco, and held it until 1971. They issued a declaration calling for the island’s return. The settlers who had occupied the island before them had left it in disrepair. Native people realized it was no longer being used and said, in effect, “We’re taking it back.” They wrote that proclamation on a piece of stretched buffalo hide.

Where did you find it?

Emma Waggoner, a graphic designer who is a citizen of the Cherokee Nation, found it. The hide was—and remains—in the collection of the U.S. Marshals Museum in Arkansas. Waggoner and her wife drove there to scout it out. They contacted the museum, though its staff was initially unsure whether they wanted to lend it to us.

I was in Santa Fe working with an archive when the archivist said, “Hang on, I know them,” and picked up the phone. He called the museum and said, “Hey, do you have this hide thing in your collection? Yeah, there’s this Native Brian Johnson who wants to get it from us.” Again, humanity is made possible by people knowing each other.

This is a key piece because it asks why Native Americans should be held to the convention of putting [design] on paper. Why would we need a huge printing press attached to the back of a horse, moving across the plains while we’re following buffalo? We can put a message on hide and put it up. And look: there’s typography and a public message, which is why this is such an important moment in the exhibition. It’s sarcastic and truthful at exactly the same time.

From the U.S. Marshals Museum—which I just learned existed—to Manhattan. How did changing the space it’s exhibited in change the object?

Here, it’s allowed to express itself, to be present and to scream. It’s not sequestered or called a prisoner; here, it has context. Is it a sacred object? No. Is it still talking to us? Yes. It’s a protest object that helped Native people gain the rights we have today.

I appreciate that Poster House cared enough to turn off the fire alarms once the show was fully installed, allowing me to sit in the institutional space. I thanked every object, especially this one, over and over. I really lived in the preparation of the room and said, “Thank you so much for being here.”

Like many pieces here, it’s attributed to ‘Designer Once Known’. In a museum, it’s more common to see on a wall text ‘Unknown artist’. What’s the nuance?

“Designer Once Known” is what we put on the label where a museum would put “Unknown.” It’s not the same thing. “Unknown” is a shrug. It’s anthropological. No way of proving it. No way of knowing. But that’s trash. The people who made that object or that work were known. They were loved. The name didn’t fall off the object. It just wasn’t valued.

“Once Known” says somebody was real, it gives them humanity again. Somebody knew whose hands cut that block, pulled that print, beaded that pennant—their name, their Nation, who taught them, their lineage, who they made it for—all the things. So when I put “Designer Once Known” on a wall, I’m not giving up on the name. I’m filing a space with dignity and the hopes of eventually one day being able to fill that in.

‘It’s Complicated’ and ‘Extractive Marketing’ are tucked in the back, a bit out of sight. What sort of work will visitors find there?

A key piece in this section was already in Poster House’s collection: a work by Winold Reiss. A German immigrant who came to the United States in the late 1880s, Reiss became an important painter during the Harlem Renaissance. He taught Aaron Douglas painting, and his portraits of Alain Locke, Langston Hughes, and Zora Neale Hurston appeared in the Met’s Harlem Renaissance exhibition.

He was also obsessed with “cowboy and Indian” stories. Went out to the Blackfeet Reservation in Montana. Got really well known there; they loved this random German guy. He paid them to sit for him, paid for a translator, painted them exactly the way they should be painted—the opposite of Edward Curtis. Painted 280 portraits. He got to know their stories and when he died, they spread his ashes on the reservation. He also sold all those paintings to the Great Northern Railroad.

And the Great Northern Railroad— ding, ding, ding —turned those portraits into marketing tools to promote its route. The company reproduced them on playing cards, business cards. None of the money went back to the reservation. Their names were not used. They were not asked for permission.

But at the same time, the typography is amazing. That’s the contradiction. The poster is beautifully made, yet it participates in a system that extracted Native people, land, and imagery for commercial gain.

It’s complicated.

It’s complicated.

Reiss ran a workshop on the reservation?

People on vacation would come to Montana and paint Native people. They were paid, but they were also treated as a bit of a sideshow, folded into the myth of the “vanishing race.” There’s something sticky about it. Why not work with them directly, or have them teach you beadwork, something from our own traditions? No, instead, it was this Michelangelo-style, grand studio. Again, the Western idea of art education.

What’s next for the show?

This is not a comprehensive show. There’s no way we could represent all 574 [federally recognized] tribes. What about the unrecognized tribes? What about the tribes that were fully erased? Which is why I’m not the only person that can speak and do this. The show needs to go somewhere like Pine Ridge, or Oklahoma City. Wherever it goes, I’d love to dig into local archives, expanding the show to fit each space. There’s a lot of Lenape material, you know, because we’re on their land. I want the people who see it to be its anchor, so it has meaning for them.

Design is fraught in many directions, as we well know, and this show has never been done before. We have to take it to underserved areas. I need Native teenagers to see that they can make these things, that they deserve to be in this space.
excerpt_original: The boundaries between craft, graphic arts, and sculpture collapse in “Designed to Be Red,” now on view at New York’s Poster House through next February.

article_text:
News

Fifth Thailand Biennale Announces Theme and Artistic Directors

JIRADEJ-PORNPILAI MEEMALAI: BAAN NOORG . Courtesy the artists.

Thailand’s Ministry of Culture has announced the artist duo jiradej-pornpilai meemalai: BAAN NOORG as the artistic directors for the fifth Thailand Biennale, scheduled to open in Rayong in December 2027. The edition will center on relationships and interconnection, framed within both local and global contexts.

Jiradej and Pornpilai Meemalai are mixed-media artists working across sculpture, video, photography, and installation. Their practice draws on the joys and hardships of their own marriage as a lens for examining the nature of human relationships more broadly, along with the way those bonds shape society and history. The duo has exhibited globally in solo and group shows spanning Taiwan, Germany, the US, and the UK, and has undertaken several international residencies including at the Headlands Center for the Arts (Sausalito, 2010), Lichtenberg Studios (Berlin, 2013), and the Civitella Ranieri Center (Umbria, 2013). They have previously participated in the 2019 Asian Art Biennial in Taichung, the 2021 Busan Sea Art Festival, and Documenta 15 in Kassel in 2022.

The duo will direct the biennale through Baan Noorg Collaborative Arts and Culture, the nonprofit artist collective they founded in 2011 in the Nongpo community of Ratchaburi province. Over the years the initiative has run residencies, workshops, exhibitions, and community programs, and has staged biennales of its own. Joining the Meemalais on the curatorial team for the Thailand Biennale are Emily Chin-Jie Lee, Gesyada Siregar, and Tyuki Imamura. Together they will present “Sin-Samudr, Turning Currents,” an exhibition exploring how art and place inform one another.

Inaugurated in 2018, each edition of the Thailand Biennale is held in a different province. Rayong sits on Thailand’s eastern seaboard and is known chiefly as a fishing and fish-sauce producing center, as well as a hub for chemical and automotive manufacturing. The location of the upcoming biennale reflects the government’s efforts to diversify and expand Thailand’s arts and cultural infrastructure beyond its major urban centers.

Harison Butler is an editorial intern at ArtAsiaPacific.
excerpt_original: The artist duo jiradej-pornpilai meemalai: BAAN NOORG will explore the theme of human relationships through local and international lenses. Harison Butler

title_original: È uscito exibart onpaper 135: da Torino a Roma, sul filo dell’immaginazione
editorial_title_zh: exibart onpaper 135期现已发布：从都灵到罗马，顺着想象力的脉络
editorial_excerpt_zh: exibart onpaper 135期飞赴都灵与罗马，聚焦 Artissima 艺博会、Arte in Nuvola 艺博会及更多精彩内容，涵盖深度报道、博物馆、艺术市场与设计，循着想象力的红线展开。文章 È uscito exibart onpaper 135: da Torino a Roma, sul filo…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在新一期的 exibart onpaper（即135期）中，贯穿着一系列主题。首先是乌托邦与想象力。此外，还有转换视角的目光、亟待重写的历史、等待被虚空填满的空间、在常规轨迹之外观察的领地。新一期 exibart 从这些坐标出发，在都灵与罗马之间穿梭，涉足博物馆、艺博会、艺术家、档案馆、艺术市场、时尚与设计。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "朱利亚·龙基（Giulia Ronchi）的社论正是以“目光”作为起点，文章由约翰·贝尔格（John Berger）的一句引文开篇，并围绕着不同的观看方式展开：向上凝视，正如迭戈·西贝利（Diego Cibelli）的作品；向东眺望，如达维德·夸德里奥（Davide Quadrio）在都灵东方艺术博物馆（MAO）的经历所呈现的那样；或者转向别处，选择改变城市与视角，正如恰恰·莱维（Ciaccia Levi）从米兰搬到都灵那样。切萨雷·比亚西尼·塞尔瓦吉（Cesare Biasini Selvaggi）的社论也回溯了乌托邦与想象力的力量，他从伊利亚·卡巴科夫（Ilya Kabakov）最具标志性的作品之一《从房间飞向宇宙的男人》切入。这是一个既不可能又极为具体的逃离意象，与本期封面的构思不谋而合。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本期封面的主角是第六届 exibart 奖得主法布里切·贝尔纳斯科尼·博尔齐（Fabrice Bernasconi Borzì），报纸内页也为他刊登了一篇专访。所选的图片来自一组三联白色翻面画布，上面写着三句话：“我不会画画”、“这就是你们将看到的一切”、“目前如此”。这是一个建立在“减法”之上的手势：剔除了图像、再现，甚至是传统上呈现给观众的画作表面，让这种虚空本身去催生无限可能。“我的创作源于一种由内而外的冲动，而非单纯应用我所学到的知识。面对自己的作品时，我发现自己始终保有一种旁观者的姿态，仿佛很好奇自己究竟能做到什么地步：所以我尝试、前行，然后驻足静观，”这位艺术家讲述道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "琳达·弗雷尼·纳格勒（Linda Fregni Nagler）的图片作品系列《Pour commander à l’air》也贯穿着一种相似的张力。艺术家搜集了20世纪50年代报纸上的照片，对其进行重新拍摄、改造和语境化重构。在这里，图像同样不是一个确凿无疑的定论，而是一个需要重新开启的场域，其中缺失的部分最终拥有与依然可见部分相同的分量。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "基于这些前提，本期杂志来到了都灵，Artissima 艺博会将于10月30日至11月1日重返该地。由路易吉·法斯（Luigi Fassi）担任艺术总监的第33届艺博会将汇聚Oval展馆内的183家意大利及国际画廊，并带来66场个展呈现。艺博会所选的主题似乎也延续了前几页展开的讨论：“想象力的杂技力量”，这一表述摘自哲学家玛莎·努斯鲍姆（Martha Nussbaum）的思想。在对艺博会的介绍中，埃尔莎·巴比耶里（Elsa Barbieri）从法斯本人提出的问题切入：“艺术如何能够充当一种至关重要的公共智能，去滋养和丰富一个社群的民主制度？”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/4.-BONUS-Artissima-2025-©-Photo-Perottino-Piva-Castellano-Bergadano.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Artissima 2025 © Photo Perottino Piva Castellano Bergadano", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "围绕着 Artissima，exibart 135期展开了大量篇幅的深度报道。保拉·普尔维伦蒂（Paola Pulvirenti）采访了达维德·夸德里奥（他目前即将卸任都灵东方艺术博物馆馆长职务），共同回顾了四年的工作历程，以及一种试图超越东西方传统割裂的博物馆理念。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "夸德里奥表示：“对我而言，极其重要的一点是打破西方与东方之间存在绝对界限的观点，转而谈论欧亚大陆：改变语言，进而改变人们的感知——这座博物馆不仅代表着我们审美品味的历程，它也是一系列欧亚关系的组成部分，这些关系由深厚且持续的历史交织而成。”因此，核心依然是改变视角，以便重新叙述历史。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一方面，玛丽亚·克里斯蒂娜·斯特拉蒂（Maria Cristina Strati）采访了 Ciaccia Levi，该画廊选择都灵来试验一种不同的画廊理念。新空间占据了由加贝蒂和伊索拉（Gabetti e Isola）设计、具有历史意义的埃拉姆波特加（Bottega d’Erasmo），并通过一种更具家庭氛围、建立在热情接待与直接交流之上的尺度，重新定义了展览空间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "扎伊拉·卡雷尔（Zaira Carrer）对比尔塔·基亚拉（Chiara Bertola）和弗吉尼亚·卢波（Virginia Lupo）两位策展人以及阿涅蒂档案馆（Archivio Agnetti）主席热尔马纳·阿涅蒂（Germana Agnetti）的采访，则聚焦于另一种形式的重新解读。访谈的起点是都灵现代艺术馆（GAM）为纪念温琴佐·阿涅蒂（Vincenzo Agnetti）诞辰百年而举办的展览《今天是一百年》（Oggi è un secolo），这也是一次回顾其研究并借助全新目录巩固对其解读契机。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为了在都灵艺术周最紧凑的日子里游刃有余，杂志再次携手 Untitled Association 制作了地图，精选了城中不容错过的活动。在 exibart 网站上，相关报道将持续每日更新，并提供针对每一天的特定参观路线。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从都灵出发前往罗马，第六届“云端罗马艺博会”（Roma Arte in Nuvola）定于11月20日至22日举行，汇集了140家意大利及国外画廊，拥有强大的机构参与阵容，今年的日程安排还延伸到了展会空间之外。其中的亮点之一便是向城市中心敞开大门。在马里奥·普拉兹故居博物馆（Casa Museo Mario Praz），由皮尔·保罗·潘科托（Pier Paolo Pancotto）构思和策划的项目《本土回响：心灵之家的当代呼应》（Echi domestici. Corrispondenze contemporanee nella casa dell’anima）将当代艺术品置于收藏历史的家具与物件之间，使不同的时代与语言产生联系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/2.-Hidetoshi-Nagasawa_Tre-cubi.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "长泽英俊（Hidetoshi Nagasawa），《三个立方体》（Tre cubi），2015年。铁。由长泽英俊档案馆提供（Courtesy Archivio Hidetoshi Nagasawa）", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "罗马也是大卫·奥利维耶罗（Davide Oliviero）采访迭戈·西贝利（Diego Cibelli）的起点，后者最近在朱利亚别墅伊特鲁里亚国家博物馆（Museo Nazionale Etrusco di Villa Giulia）揭幕了一件永久瓷质装置作品。该作品借鉴了古代的形态并将其转化为当代的可能性，在其创作实践中，艺术生产往往伴随着与社区和学校的合作。“在谈到我的作品时，我经常听到有人问：‘难道你不怕它碎吗？’而我总是想：‘碎的不是瓷器，而是面对复杂性时的各种关系。’我喜欢将我的艺术创作视作一场可能的晚宴，这里的菜品从来不会吝啬，”这位那不勒斯艺术家如是说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "同样针对罗马，《exibart》135期推出了与无名协会（Untitled Association）合作制作的地图，从而为都灵和首都的艺术周构建了一份双重指南。我们也将亲临这两座城市，在都灵艺博会（Artissima）和云端罗马艺博会（Arte in Nuvola）设立《exibart》展位。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但本期杂志也关注了近几个月来将藏品安全重新推回辩论核心的主题之一。瓦伦蒂娜·卡萨基亚（Valentina Casacchia）的文章从几起轰动一时的新闻事件切入——从2025年10月卢浮宫失窃案，到2026年8月墨西拿MuMe博物馆安托内洛·达·梅西那（Antonello Da Messina）的《多联画》（Polittico）失窃案——以此深入探讨博物馆盗窃案的动态：什么被盗、为什么某些物件比其他物件更有吸引力，以及盗窃一件艺术品与盗窃可以被拆分并更容易重新投放市场的珠宝之间有什么区别。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对过去的审视也回到了各个专栏中。在致力于艺术市场的板块中，埃里卡·罗切拉（Erica Roccella）探讨了人们对古代艺术重新燃起的兴趣，汇聚了致力于古代大师（Old Masters）和古董的主要艺博会的声音。近年来，该行业一直在寻找新的叙事形式以及与当代收藏关系的新模式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在时尚方面，费代里科·波莱蒂（Federico Poletti）则观察了三个国际品牌——Victor-Hart、Saman Loira和Unknown Artisan——在这些品牌中，与传统、技术以及工匠知识的关系成为了构建新语言的素材。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/3.-UNKNOWN-ARTISAN-7Foto-Alex-Allegra.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Unknown Artisan，摄影：亚历克斯·阿莱格拉（Alex Allegra）", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "设计版块前瞻了将于2026年11月14日至2027年3月29日在威尼斯佩姬·古根海姆收藏馆（Collezione Peggy Guggenheim）举办的展览《天使的锻造厂。佩姬·古根海姆与20世纪艺术玻璃》（Fucina degli Angeli. Peggy Guggenheim e il vetro artistico del Novecento），该展览展示并重构了20世纪收藏史与玻璃制造史上的一个特殊篇章。马尔科·佩特罗尼（Marco Petroni）则深入探讨了由伊诺第出版社（Einaudi）出版的芭芭拉·卡内瓦利（Barbara Carnevali）与埃马努埃莱·昆茨（Emanuele Quinz）合著的《1954-1989年意大利设计理论》（Teorie del design in Italia 1954-1989）：重构了长达三十多年的历史，在此期间，意大利的设计不仅是物件和形态的生产，也是理论、批评和政治阐述的沃土。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一如既往，本期杂志以卢安娜·贝尔蒂（Luciana Berti）的星座运势（exibastro）收尾，这一次，它通过都灵和皮埃蒙特伟大名人的星象指引着艺术人生。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《exibart》135期正在都灵和罗马、都灵艺博会和云端罗马艺博会以及全意大利的艺术与文化空间中发行。此外，读者还可以在线购买单期杂志或进行订阅。", "links": [{"text": "singolo numero", "url": "https://service.exibart.com/prodotto/on-paper-n-135/"}, {"text": "abbonamento", "url": "https://service.exibart.com/prodotto/abbonamento-onpaper-digitale/"}], "translated": true}]

article_text:
C’è una costellazione di temi che attraversa il nostro nuovo exibart onpaper, il 135. Utopia e immaginazione, innanzitutto. Ma anche sguardi che cambiano direzione, storie da riscrivere, spazi da riempire di vuoto, territori da osservare fuori dalle traiettorie consuete. Il nuovo numero di exibart parte da queste coordinate e si muove tra Torino e Roma, passando per musei, fiere, artisti, archivi, mercato, moda e design.

È proprio lo sguardo il punto di partenza dell’editoriale di Giulia Ronchi , aperto da una citazione di John Berger e costruito attorno a diversi modi di guardare: verso l’alto, come nel lavoro di Diego Cibelli ; verso Est, come propone Davide Quadrio nella sua esperienza al MAO di Torino; oppure altrove, scegliendo di cambiare città e prospettiva, come ha fatto Ciaccia Levi trasferendosi da Milano a Torino. All’utopia e alla forza dell’immaginazione torna anche l’editoriale di Cesare Biasini Selvaggi , che prende le mosse da una delle opere più emblematiche di Ilya Kabakov , L’uomo che volò nel cosmo dalla sua stanza . Un’immagine di fuga impossibile e insieme concretissima, che si collega idealmente alla copertina di questo numero.

Protagonista della cover è Fabrice Bernasconi Borzì , vincitore della sesta edizione dell’exibart prize, al quale è dedicata anche un’intervista all’interno del giornale. L’immagine scelta proviene da un trittico di tele bianche voltate, sulle quali compaiono tre frasi: «Non so ancora dipingere», «Questo è tutto ciò che vedrete», «Per il momento.». Un gesto fondato sulla sottrazione: si tolgono immagine, rappresentazione e perfino la superficie pittorica tradizionalmente offerta allo spettatore, lasciando che sia proprio quel vuoto a produrre possibilità. «Il mio lavoro nasce da un impulso sentito, non dalla semplice applicazione di ciò che studio. Mi accorgo, di fronte alla mia opera, di rimanere sempre un po’ spettatore di me stesso, come se fossi curioso di vedere di cosa sono capace: perciò provo, vado avanti e poi resto a vedere», racconta l’artista.

Una tensione analoga attraversa le pagine di apertura affidate alle immagini di Linda Fregni Nagler , con la serie Pour commander à l’air . L’artista recupera fotografie provenienti da giornali degli anni Cinquanta, le rifotografa, le riadatta e le ricontestualizza. Anche qui l’immagine non è un dato definitivo ma un luogo da riaprire, nel quale ciò che manca finisce per avere lo stesso peso di ciò che rimane visibile.

Da queste premesse il numero approda a Torino, dove dal 30 ottobre al 1° novembre torna Artissima . La 33ma edizione, diretta da Luigi Fassi , riunisce all’Oval 183 gallerie italiane e internazionali, con 66 presentazioni monografiche. Anche il tema scelto dalla fiera sembra proseguire il discorso avviato nelle prime pagine: la «Forza acrobatica dell’immaginazione», espressione tratta dal pensiero della filosofa Martha Nussbaum . Nell’introduzione alla fiera, Elsa Barbieri parte dall’interrogativo posto dallo stesso Fassi: «In che modo l’arte può agire come un’intelligenza pubblica cruciale, capace di nutrire e arricchire le istituzioni democratiche di una comunità?».

Attorno ad Artissima si sviluppa una parte consistente di exibart 135. Paola Pulvirenti incontra Davide Quadrio, ormai verso la conclusione del suo mandato al MAO – Museo d’Arte Orientale di Torino , per parlare di quattro anni di lavoro e di una concezione del museo che tenta di superare la tradizionale separazione tra Oriente e Occidente.

«Un elemento per me di grande interesse è quello di abbattere l’idea di una separazione netta tra Occidente-Oriente e di parlare, invece, di continente eurasiatico: cambiare il linguaggio, e di conseguenza la percezione del fatto che non solo questo museo rappresenta la storia del nostro gusto, ma fa parte anche di tutta una serie di relazioni che sono eurasiatiche, costituite da una storia profonda e costante», racconta Quadrio. Ancora una volta, dunque, il punto è cambiare prospettiva per poter ri-raccontare la storia.

Maria Cristina Strati intervista invece Ciaccia Levi, che ha scelto Torino per sperimentare una diversa idea di galleria. La nuova sede occupa la storica Bottega d’Erasmo progettata da Gabetti e Isola e ridefinisce lo spazio espositivo attraverso una dimensione più domestica, costruita sull’accoglienza e sulla relazione diretta.

A un’altra forma di rilettura è dedicata l’intervista di Zaira Carrer alle curatrici Chiara Bertola e Virginia Lupo , insieme a Germana Agnetti , presidente dell’Archivio Agnetti. Punto di partenza è Oggi è un secolo , la mostra della GAM di Torino dedicata a Vincenzo Agnetti nel centenario della nascita, occasione per tornare sulla sua ricerca e per consolidarne la lettura anche attraverso un nuovo catalogo.

Per orientarsi nei giorni più intensi della Torino dell’arte, tornano poi le mappe realizzate con Untitled Association , con una selezione degli appuntamenti da non perdere in città. Sul sito di exibart il racconto proseguirà quotidianamente, con itinerari specifici per ciascuna giornata.

Da Torino si va a Roma, dove dal 20 al 22 novembre è in programma la sesta edizione di Roma Arte in Nuvola , con 140 gallerie italiane e straniere, una forte presenza istituzionale e un programma che quest’anno si estende anche fuori dagli spazi della fiera. Tra le novità c’è infatti l’apertura verso il centro della città. Alla Casa Museo Mario Praz , Echi domestici. Corrispondenze contemporanee nella casa dell’anima , progetto ideato e curato da Pier Paolo Pancotto , inserisce opere contemporanee tra gli arredi e gli oggetti della collezione storica, mettendo in relazione tempi e linguaggi differenti.

Roma è anche il punto di partenza dell’intervista di Davide Oliviero a Diego Cibelli, che ha recentemente inaugurato un’installazione permanente in porcellana al Museo Nazionale Etrusco di Villa Giulia . L’opera riprende forme provenienti dall’antico per trasformarle in possibilità contemporanee, all’interno di una pratica nella quale la produzione artistica si accompagna spesso al lavoro con comunità e scuole. «In relazione al mio lavoro, mi sento spesso chiedere: “Ma non hai paura che si rompa?”. E io penso sempre: “Non è la porcellana a rompersi, ma i rapporti di fronte alle complessità”. Amo guardare alla mia produzione artistica come a un possibile invito a cena, dove non c’è mai risparmio sulle portate», racconta l’artista napoletano.

Anche per Roma, exibart 135 propone una mappa realizzata con Untitled Association, costruendo così una doppia guida alle settimane dell’arte di Torino e della Capitale. E noi saremo presenti fisicamente in entrambe le città, con gli stand di exibart ad Artissima e ad Arte in Nuvola.

Ma il numero guarda anche a uno dei temi che negli ultimi mesi ha riportato al centro del dibattito la sicurezza delle collezioni. Nell’articolo di Valentina Casacchia , si parte da eclatanti casi di cronaca, dal furto del Louvre dell’ottobre 2025 a quello dell’agosto 2026 del Polittico di Antonello Da Messina al museo MuMe di Messina, per un approfondimento sulle dinamiche dei furti museali: che cosa viene rubato, perché alcuni oggetti sono più appetibili di altri e che cosa cambia tra il furto di un’opera d’arte e quello di gioielli, che possono essere smembrati e reimmessi più facilmente sul mercato.

Lo sguardo sul passato torna anche nelle rubriche. Nella sezione dedicata al mercato dell’arte, Erica Roccella indaga il rinnovato interesse per l’arte antica, riunendo le voci delle principali fiere dedicate agli Old Masters e all’antiquariato. Un settore che negli ultimi anni sta cercando nuove forme di racconto e un nuovo rapporto con il collezionismo contemporaneo.

Sul versante della moda, Federico Poletti osserva invece tre esperienze internazionali – Victor-Hart, Saman Loira e Unknown Artisan – nelle quali il rapporto con la tradizione, le tecniche e il sapere artigianale diventa materiale per costruire nuovi linguaggi.

La sezione design anticipa Fucina degli Angeli. Peggy Guggenheim e il vetro artistico del Novecento , in programma dal 14 novembre 2026 al 29 marzo 2027 alla Collezione Peggy Guggenheim di Venezia , mostra che ricostruisce un capitolo particolare della storia del collezionismo e della produzione vetraria del XX secolo. Marco Petroni approfondisce invece Teorie del design in Italia 1954-1989 di Barbara Carnevali ed Emanuele Quinz , pubblicato da Einaudi: una ricostruzione di oltre trent’anni durante i quali il design italiano non fu soltanto produzione di oggetti e forme ma anche terreno di elaborazione teorica, critica e politica.

A chiudere il numero, come sempre, l’exibastro di Luciana Berti , che questa volta orienta le vite d’arte attraverso le stelle di grandi personalità torinesi e piemontesi.

exibart onpaper 135 è in distribuzione a Torino e Roma, ad Artissima e Roma Arte in Nuvola, e negli spazi dedicati all’arte e alla cultura in tutta Italia. È inoltre possibile acquistarlo online, come singolo numero oppure in abbonamento .

"“本次展览中，我也介绍了自己实际前往首尔驻留时遇到的艺术家。在考察她们、他们的创作过程与作品共同点的过程中，我注意到，每个人都以自身的身体经验为轴，一边凝视现实世界、人的存在以及‘此刻在此存在’究竟意味着什么，一边进行创作。”（吉田）", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/662bd849/c0669cd5-09c9-429d-a564-1222b309cf9a.jpg?q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "“TOKAS Project Vol. 9《存在的重演》”视觉图", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“重演”主要是戏剧与表演艺术中使用的词。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“之所以选择‘重演’而非‘再现’，是因为‘再现’是将某一事象原样地作为形象来表象；而本展希望呈现的实践是，每位艺术家以自身身体重新把握其所观察到的现实世界与生命的存在方式，并伴随新的解释，再次动态地使其在场显现。我们将这一行为理解为‘重演’。”（吉田）", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "三野新：登上斜面舞台，体验戏曲《温室／온실》", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览从三野新的装置所在的1楼开始。平时平坦的空间里搭起了斜面舞台。照片像挂毯一样从天花板垂下，扬声器上则放置着“石”“铁”“卡车”的照片，构成一件装置。观众可以在空间内自由走动，也可以登上舞台。三野既是摄影师也是舞台创作者，他将场所与物件上残留的风景连接起来，以自己拍摄的照片和影像为基础创作虚构，并以演出形式展开作品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "去年，三野在首尔的SeMA南智驻留项目驻留，研究了韩国龙山美军基地以及战后占领时期的历史。他由此考察战争如何影响当下的日常生活与身体，并基于成果新写了戏曲《温室／온실（Onsil）》，以装置形式进行演出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/8effe8ae/ddd8ca59-d9d6-4fb3-825f-450fbf218fee.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "会场风景之一，三野新《温室／온실（Onsil）》展示风景　摄影：高桥健治　图片提供：Tokyo Arts and Space　[＊]", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“作品采用了所谓物件剧场的手法，即不以人类，而以日用品或既有物品作为登场人物来上演舞台。扬声器中发出前述‘石’‘铁’‘卡车’的声音。它们讲述的是‘无法停止的故事’。而且它们无法卸下自己的角色。这部戏曲让人感到，这也映照出我们人类同样无法卸下自己的角色。”（吉田）", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "空间分为两个房间，虽然艺术家并未明言，但构成上会让观众从这分隔开的2个房间联想到巡游日本与韩国的情景。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这是三野先生说过的话：希望大家能以来看戏剧的感觉来观看。希望观众在舞台中巡游，自身也作为某种出演者参与舞台，进入故事之中。”（吉田）", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "金度希：为人们的肚脐取模，连缀成山", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "上到2楼，前方的小空间里展示着金度希的作品。形状歪斜的山形石膏像排列着，天花板垂下形状相同、略微放大的金属钟，观众也可以实际敲响。墙上也贴着相似造型物的照片。这些都是以人的肚脐取模制成的。", "肚脐人人都有，但很多人并不知道他人的肚脐是什么形状。从外部看不见的内部结构，因人而完全不同。被取模而成的群山，展现出这种多样性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": {"type": "paragraph", "text": "据吉田介绍，金本人身为母亲也是该项目的背景之一。肚脐被视为能够体感分娩以及人与人之间联结的身体一部分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "取模的方法是，请遇到的人躺下，将石膏灌入肚脐。金不仅复制形状，也珍视取模行为中产生的沟通。据说她至今创造了能够体感与无数人生命联结的场所。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我想介绍艺术家围绕一个主题持续发展、长期投入的珍贵活动。作品具有将观众卷入其中的存在感与力量，希望大家能亲身感受。”（吉田）", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/8ef4ad55/23d1561b-1b17-4706-b5ad-2eb6d9aee38b.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "会场风景之一，金度希《Navel "本作是一个项目：将京剧名旦梅兰芳留下的、以照片记录表现旦角的12种姿态与53种手势的珍贵记录集，经由殷自己的身体重新翻译。殷不仅查阅资料，还前往被视为京剧重镇的武汉与北京，在继承梅兰芳流派的师父门下学习表演与舞蹈。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「過去に生きていた存在を、アーティスト自身の身体で現代によみがえらせるような、フィジカルなアプローチによって、存在というものをとらえていく表現を紹介したいと考えました」（吉田）"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "ク・ドンヒ：新作の中で、旧作が「再演」される"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "大画面で映し出される新作の映像作品《Cascade（カスケード）》は、水路や橋を起点に、自身と他者が撮影した異なる文脈の映像をサンプリングして構成した作品だ。そのスクリーンの右下にはモニターが埋め込まれ、旧作《Under the Vein; I spell on you（静脈の下、あなたに魔法をかける）》が映し出されている。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "なお、会期中にはトークイベントや、三野新のインスタレーションを実際に役者が演じる演劇パフォーマンスなど、関連イベントも数多く開催される。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "5名が身体を起点に立ち上げた「再演」を、フロアを上がりながら体験してみよう。"}]
article_text:
Sponsored by トーキョーアーツアンドスペース（TOKAS）

トーキョーアーツアンドスペース本郷（TOKAS本郷） で、 「TOKAS Project Vol. 9『在ることの再演』」 が10月3日からスタートした。会期は11月8日まで。 ウン・ジェピル、キム・ドヒ、ク・ドンヒ、パク・ミンハ、三野新 の日韓5名のアーティストが、自身の身体経験をもとに現実や生のありようを展示空間に立ち上げる作品を発表している。

「在ること」とは、「再演」とは何か？ 担当学芸員の 吉田紗和子 に作品や展覧会について話を聞いた。

「再現」ではなく「再演」である理由

同時代の表現を東京から創造・発信するアートセンター・TOKASは、展覧会などを行なうTOKAS本郷と、滞在制作やリサーチ活動を行うTOKASレジデンシー（墨田区）の2拠点を持ち、国内外のアーティストのサポートを行っている。

本展は国際的な交流を促進し、多文化的な視点で多様なテーマについて思考する展覧会プログラム「TOKAS Project」の9回目にあたる。TOKASでは2006年より、ソウルの機関と相互にアーティストを派遣してきた。その交流が20周年を迎えたことを記念し、出展作家は過去にTOKASのレジデンス・プログラムに参加した日韓の作家を中心に構成されている。

「この展覧会では、私が実際にソウルのレジデンシーに足を運び、そこで出会ったアーティストも紹介しています。彼女ら、彼らの制作プロセスや作品の共通点を考察していくうちに、それぞれが自身の身体経験を軸に、現実の世界や人間という存在、“いまここに在る”とはどういうことなのかを見つめながら制作している点に着目しました」（吉田）

「再演」は、演劇やパフォーミングアーツで主に使われる言葉だ。

「『再現』ではなく、『再演』という言葉を選んだのは、『再現』はある事象をそのままイメージとして表象するのに対し、本展では、それぞれのアーティストが観察した現実の世界や生のありようを、自身の身体をもってとらえ直し、新たな解釈を伴って再びこの場に動的に現前化していく、という実践を示したかったからです。その行為を『再演』としてとらえています」（吉田）

三野新：斜面の舞台に上がり、戯曲『温室／온실』を体験する

展覧会は、三野新のインスタレーションがある1階から始まる。普段はフラットなスペースには、斜面の舞台が組まれている。天井からタペストリーのように写真が吊り下げられ、「石」、「鉄」、「トラック」の写真がスピーカーの上に設置されたインスタレーションだ。来場者は空間内を自由に歩き回り、舞台の上にも上がることができる。写真家であり舞台作家でもある三野は、場所やものに残る風景をつなぎ、自ら撮影した写真や映像をもとにフィクションを制作、上演という形式で作品を展開してきた。

昨年、三野はソウルのSeMAナンジ・レジデンシーに滞在し、韓国の龍山米軍基地や戦後の占領期に関する歴史をリサーチした。そして、戦争が現在の日常生活や身体にどのような影響を及ぼしているかを考察、その成果をもとに戯曲『温室／온실（オンシル）』を書き下ろし、インスタレーションとして上演する。

「作品としてはオブジェクト・シアターという、人間ではなく、日用品や既存のモノを登場人物に見立てて舞台を上演する手法を用いています。スピーカーからは、前述した『石』と『鉄』と『トラック』の声が発せられます。彼らによって語られるのは、『やめることができない物語』です。そして、彼らはその役を降りることができません。そのことが、私たち人間も、自分の役を降りることはできないということを映し出しているように感じさせられる戯曲です」（吉田）

空間はふたつの部屋に分かれており、作家は明言はしていないものの、鑑賞者はその分かれた2部屋に日本と韓国を巡る情景を思い浮かべる構成となっている。

「三野さんが言っていたことですが、演劇を見に来る感覚で見てもらえると良いですね。舞台のなかをめぐりながら、鑑賞者自身もある種の出演者として舞台に参加し、物語のなかに入り込んでほしいです」（吉田）

キム・ドヒ：人々のおへそを型取り、山を連ねる

2階に上がり、手前の小さいスペースにキム・ドヒの作品が展示されている。いびつな山のかたちをした石膏像が並び、天井からは同じかたちをやや拡大した金属の鐘が吊られており、鑑賞者は実際に鳴らすこともできる。壁にも、似た造形物の写真が貼られている。これらはすべて、人のおへそを型取ったものだ。

「キム・ドヒは2018年にTOKASのレジデンス・プログラムに参加し、その滞在をきっかけに、人間の生命の根源の象徴として、おへそに着目しました。そして人々とコミュニケーションを築く手段として、彼らのおへそを石膏で型取るプロジェクト『Navel Mountain （へその山）』を継続的に行っています」（吉田）

現在までに、キムは日本や韓国の各地で100人以上のおへそを型取っているという。

おへそは誰もが持っているものでありながら、他人のおへそがどんなかたちなのかを多くの人は知らない。外からは見えない奥の構造は、人によってまったく違う。型取られた山々は、その多様さを見せてくれる。

吉田によれば、キム自身が母親であることもプロジェクトの背景にある。おへそは、出産や、人と人とのつながりを体感できる身体の一部としてとらえられた。

型取りの方法は、出会った人に横たわってもらい、おへそに石膏を流し込むというものだ。かたちを写しとるだけでなく、型取る行為のなかで生まれるコミュニケーションも、キムは大切にしている。これまで、無数の人々との生のつながりを体感できる場を作ってきたのだという。

「アーティストがひとつのテーマを発展させながら長期的に取り組む、その貴重な活動を紹介したいと思いました。鑑賞者を取り込むような作品の存在感や強さもあり、それを体感してほしいです」（吉田）

パク・ミンハ：計算の世界に、蛾が迷い込む

奥へ進むと、パク・ミンハの映像インスタレーションが広がる。最初に目にするのは、NASAの火星の画像アーカイヴをもとにした《Shadow Planet（影の惑星）》、そしてベルリン自然史博物館と協働して制作した、ブラキオサウルスの化石による語りを軸に展開される《Time Paradox（タイム・パラドックス）》だ。パクはメディア技術や科学的な復元のなかに潜む「イメージの政治性」を明らかにすることで、私たちを取り巻く枠組みに疑問を投げかける作品を作り続けてきた。

今回、パクは新作《Bug（バグ）》を発表する。二分割された画面の左側には、ロボットが強化学習のシミュレーションで訓練を受ける様子、右側には一匹の蛾が偶然データセンターに迷い込む様子が映し出される。迷い込んだ蛾（バグ）によって、機械的な計算の世界には少しずつエラー（バグ）が引き起こされていく。

「効率性を求める計算的な世界に、蛾という、命あるものが迷い込むところから作品は始まります。蛾が迷い込むことで、アルゴリズムが変わっていき、ロボットの動きも変わっていきます。AIやロボットに人間の労働が代替されている時代において、生命とは何か、人間性や人間のフィジカリティとは何かということを問いかけてくる作品です」（吉田）

ウン・ジェピル：京劇俳優・梅蘭芳の身体を、自分の身体で翻訳し直す

3階の展示はウン・ジェピルの作品から始まる。ウンは伝統と現代性、男性と女性など概念の境界を解体する試みを続けているアーティストだ。本展では、中国の伝統演劇、京劇の女形をテーマにした《Blue Night, Blue Shadows（青い夜、青い影）》を展示する。

本作は京劇の名女形・梅蘭芳が残した女形を表現する12のポージングと53の手の動きを写真付きで収めた希少な記録集を、ウン自身の身体を介して新たに翻訳し直すプロジェクトだ。ウンは資料にあたるだけでなく、京劇の拠点とされる武漢と北京へ渡り、梅蘭芳の流派を受け継ぐ師匠のもとで演技と踊りを学んだ。

「彼は実際にこの梅蘭芳の流派で踊りも演技も学び、訓練したうえで、記録集の梅蘭芳の所作を自身で体現して写真に撮影し、銅板に刻み、印刷して、最後に一冊の本に編纂しました。さらに、それをライブで表現するパフォーマンスも行っています」（吉田）

会場には、銅板に刻まれた手の動きや、それを刷った版画、衣装が並ぶ。ウンはこれらを通して、クロスジェンダーな感覚も探る。舞台に置かれた椅子のスピーカーからは、パフォーマンスの際の繊細な足音が聞こえてくる。

「過去に生きていた存在を、アーティスト自身の身体で現代によみがえらせるような、フィジカルなアプローチによって、存在というものをとらえていく表現を紹介したいと考えました」（吉田）

ク・ドンヒ：新作の中で、旧作が「再演」される

3階の奥は、ク・ドンヒの映像インスタレーションだ。ク・ドンヒは、TOKASのレジデンス・プログラムが始まって2年目の2007年に参加した。日常の出来事や、テレビ、インターネットで収集した情報の断片を再構成して映像を組み立て、そこに不条理な要素を忍ばせる手法を用いる作品で知られる。

大画面で映し出される新作の映像作品《Cascade（カスケード）》は、水路や橋を起点に、自身と他者が撮影した異なる文脈の映像をサンプリングして構成した作品だ。そのスクリーンの右下にはモニターが埋め込まれ、旧作《Under the Vein; I spell on you（静脈の下、あなたに魔法をかける）》が映し出されている。

「情報化社会のなかで、情報が処理されていくプロセスに焦点を当てた作品です。実際にクさんが撮った映像もありますし、漢江に橋が作られたときの実際のニュースやドキュメンタリー映像など、いろんな映像が組み合わされています」（吉田）

画面の右下に映し出されている旧作には、滝の水脈を探し、ダウジングをしながら歩く男が登場する。彼が探し当てた水源は、じつは水道の蛇口で、滝は人工のものだったという結末で終わる。

「《Cascade（カスケード）》の画面の中に旧作を再演することで、旧作を再考察する意味合いも持っています」（吉田）

過去と現在が交錯し、様々なイメージがとめどなく流れていく本作には、情報の量と流れに翻弄される現代の私たちの状況を重ね合わせることもできるだろう。

5名の作家たちは、様々な切り口で作家を取り巻く状況を再演している。

「今回の5名の芸術の実践を通して、私たちの想像力や視点が刷新されていくような面白さを体感してほしいです。展覧会をご覧になったあとも、作品で描かれているテーマが、今度は鑑賞者の方自身の解釈で、能動的に再演されていくのではないかと考えています」（吉田）

なお、会期中にはトークイベントや、三野新のインスタレーションを実際に役者が演じる演劇パフォーマンスなど、関連イベントも数多く開催される。

5名が身体を起点に立ち上げた「再演」を、フロアを上がりながら体験してみよう。

article_text:
写真家・北村圭介の個展「巡る」が、2026年10月29日（木）から11月17日（火）まで、東京・目黒のBOOK AND SONSで開催される。展覧会に合わせて、同名の写真集『巡る』も刊行される。

本展では、子どもの頃の断片的で曖昧な記憶をテーマに、北村が自身の子どもたちとの日々を撮り続けてきた作品を紹介する。何気ない日常の風景や、いつか忘れてしまうかもしれない瞬間。子どもたちの成長とともに移り変わる時間を写真にとどめながら、過去の記憶と現在の風景が重なり合う感覚を浮かび上がらせる。

記憶は時とともに曖昧になり、写真はその一瞬を残し続ける。身近な家族との時間を通して、記憶と時間の境界を静かに問いかける展覧会となる。

タイトル

北村圭介 写真展「巡る」

場所

BOOK AND SONS（東京都目黒区鷹番2-13-3 キャトル鷹番）

会期

2026年10月29日（木）〜11月17日（火）

時間

12:00〜19:00

休み

水曜日

料金

無料

URL

http://www.kitamurakeisuke.com/

article_text:
Roxy Cinema A print of Society and live-scored editions of Nosferatu & Vampyr play on Friday; The Guyver , No Picnic , and a print of Freaked screen on Saturday, which brings City Dudes ; a shorts program shows on Sunday.

Museum of Modern Art A Sergei Loznitsa retrospective begins this weekend.

BAM Ken Russell’s reconstructed The Devils continues—read (or listen to) our interview with Mark Kermode on it.

Film Forum A celebration of William Greaves’ centennial begins; Corpse Bride shows on Sunday.

Anthology Film Archives A Troma series begins.

Museum of the Moving Image Persona shows on Friday; The Exorcist and a print of Bram Stoker’s Dracula are featured in Handcrafted Horror; Vampire’s Kiss shows on 35mm on Saturday; Richard Attenborough’s Magic plays on 35mm Sunday.

IFC Center Hellraiser begins playing in a new 4K restoration; Ken Russell’s reconstructed The Devils continues on a restored 35mm print—read (or listen to) our interview with Mark Kermode on it—while The Exorcist , Grey Gardens , Ju-On: The Grudge , and Redline play late.

Nitehawk Prospect Park Ginger Snaps screens early on Saturday and Sunday.

Metrograph All That Heaven Allows , Peppermint Frappé , Brief Encounter , Strangers on a Train , Something Special , The Addams Family , Girl Interrupted , and The Flavor of Green Tea Over Rice show on 35mm while Virgina starts showing in a restoration; Terence Fisher starts while The Leaves are Falling , Trains: Local Routes , Classical Cinema , and Darius Khondji continue.

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "下周，4月27日星期一，林肯中心电影协会将授予乔治·克鲁尼年度卓别林奖。自1990年代以来，克鲁尼一直是美国媒体星空中的一颗耀眼明星，从他在《急诊室的故事》中的突破性角色，到无数热门作品，如《逃狱三王》（2000）、《十一罗汉》（2001）、《迈克尔·克莱顿》（2007）、《后人》（2011），仅举几例——再到诺亚·鲍姆巴赫近期的《杰伊·凯利》（2025），他在片中奉献了一场闪烁而自反的表演，饰演一位回望漫长而辉煌职业生涯中所做选择的电影明星。无论角色大小，还是导演作品，克鲁尼都将多才多艺、谦逊、幽默和坚定的道德信念结合在一起，并拥有无可否认的银幕存在感。", "links": [{"text": "Chaplin Award", "url": "https://www.filmlinc.org/chaplin-award-gala/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "亚当·奈曼在为本周五发布的《电影评论通讯》撰写的一篇文章中写道：“宝琳·凯尔在她最后一次公开接受采访时曾称赞克鲁尼在《夺金三王》（1999）中的表演（‘他非常出色’），她曾称加里·格兰特为‘来自梦幻之城的人’。克鲁尼的才华让这句话反了过来。他不是凭空显现，而是脚踏实地、扎根大地——不是幻想中的人物，而是恶作剧的执着者。克鲁尼一贯被安排扮演小贼、骗子和道德上灵活的专业人士，他穿行于熟悉的演员领地，并仅凭存在感的力量将其转化。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在下周卓别林奖晚会之前，《电影评论》编辑德维卡·吉里什与克鲁尼聊了他的职业生涯的深度与广度——他的关键角色、他的创作方法，以及他带给每一场表演和每一部作品的世界观。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Next week, on Monday, April 27, Film at Lincoln Center honors George Clooney with their annual Chaplin Award . Clooney has been a shining star in the American media firmament since the 1990s, from his breakout role on E.R. , through innumerable hits, like O Brother, Where Art Thou (2000), Ocean’s Eleven (2001), Michael Clayton (2007), The Descendants (2011), just to name a few—to Noah Baumbach’s recent Jay Kelly (2025), in which he gave a twinkling, reflexive performance as a movie star looking back on the choices made during a long and illustrious career. Throughout roles big and small, as well as directorial outings, Clooney has combined versatility, humility, humor, and strong moral convictions, with an undeniable screen presence.

Adam Nayman writes in an essay for The Film Comment Letter, dropping this Friday: “Pauline Kael, who shouted out Clooney’s performance in Three Kings (1999) in her final on-the-record interview (‘he was very good’), once called Cary Grant ‘The Man From Dream City.’ Clooney’s gifts put that phrase in reverse. Instead of materializing out of thin air, he’s grounded, earthbound—not a figure of fantasy but a stickler for mischief. Tasked consistently with playing petty thieves, swindlers, and ethically flexible professional types, Clooney traverses familiar actorly terrain and transforms it, by sheer force of presence.”

In advance of next week’s Chaplin Award Gala, Film Comment Editor Devika Girish chatted with Clooney about the depth and breadth of his career—his key roles, his approach to his craft, and his vision of the world which he brings to every performance and work.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE : Ron Livingston ( The Conjuring ), Beverly D’Angelo ( American History X ) and Omar Benson Miller ( Sinners ) will star with Tyrese Gibson ( Fast & Furious franchise) in writer-director Deon Taylor’s horror film Don’t Open the Door.

Oscar-nominated producer and long-time Quentin Tarantino collaborator Shannon McIntosh ( Once Upon a Time in Hollywood ) and NFL star Cameron ‘Cam’ Heyward are partnering with Taylor and Roxanne Avent’s Hidden Empire Film Group to produce the movie.

Shannon is producing through her McIntosh Films banner and Heyward via his new Iron 97 Productions label. Maxime Alexandre ( The Nun ) is aboard as cinematographer.

Related Stories

Ron Livingston Joins Alex Borstein & June Squibb In Dramedy 'Turn The Lights Back On'

Briarcliff Closes Domestic On 'Christmas At The Kringles' For Holiday Wide Release

Plot details are being kept under wraps but will deal with “real-world trauma”. Principle photography begins this week in Mississippi. The filmmakers say they are also launching a graphic novel-inspired universe that will work to push the story beyond the screen.

Watch on Deadline

Director Deon Taylor, whose films include Fatale , Black & Blue and The Intruder , said: “ Don’t Open the Door is going to scare audiences like they’ve never been scared before and the performances of Ron, Beverly and Omar, alongside Tyrese are what’s going to make that happen. They each bring important layers very much needed in a story as twisted as this. Having this group anchor our movie and welcoming partners Shannon and Cam into the production has as us as more excited than ever.”

Ron Livingston is represented by UTA, Thruline Entertainment and Hansen, Jacobson. Beverly D’Angelo is represented by IAG and MPE. Omar Benson is represented by IAG and Mainstay Entertainment. Deon Taylor, Roxanne Avent Taylor and Hidden Empire Film Group are represented by CAA.
